aboutTempleContent1: Shri Kshetra Macchindranath Sanjivani Samadhi Mandir is a revered temple located in Sawaragaon, Ashti, in the Beed district of Maharashtra. The temple is dedicated to Lord Macchindranath, a revered saint and spiritual figure. The temple is known for its serene atmosphere and spiritual significance, attracting devotees from all over the region. It serves as a place of worship, meditation, and community gatherings, fostering a sense of devotion and spirituality among its visitors.
aboutTempleContent2: The saga of Lord Machhindranath (also known as Matsyendranath) begins in the primordial era. According to the sacred Puranas, while Lord Shiva (Adinath) was revealing the secret of Brahmavidya and Yoga to Goddess Parvati on the banks of the cosmic ocean, a fish in the water listened with absolute stillness and devotion. Upon realizing the fish had attained divine enlightenment, Lord Shiva transformed it into a celestial mahayogi. Thus, he was named Machhindranath—the first human Guru of the Nath Sampradaya, born directly from the grace of Mahadev.

On this auspicious occasion, a grand Chhabina procession and traditional Hanganma celebrations are held, as devotees gather with deep devotion to offer prayers and seek divine blessings at the Samadhi Sthal. The temple is beautifully decorated, and special rituals are performed to commemorate this auspicious occasion.

aboutMandirText1: Located on the sacred hill of Machindranath Gad at Mayamba (Savaragaon) in Maharashtra, the revered Machindranath Sanjeevan Samadhi Temple is one of the most spiritually powerful centers of the Nath sect.
aboutMandirText2: The very thought of visiting Shri Sadguru Machindranath fills the heart with divine joy and devotion. A unique spiritual attraction pulls the mind towards this place. Devotees come to Machindranath Gad with deep faith, offering their heartfelt emotions at the feet of the divine, and experience immense peace and bliss. Even in Kaliyuga, this place remains highly awakened and is situated atop the Garbhagiri mountain.
aboutMandirText3: The Samadhi site of Shri Machindranath is located 8 km south of Madhi Kanifnath and 3 km north of Savaragaon on the Garbhagiri mountain. One has to climb the hill from Madhi, using steps on foot. There are multiple routes to reach the fort, and now a new road connects Madhi to Mayamba. The path is surrounded by dense forests and scenic beauty. The waterfall here is known as Mayamba Falls and attracts many nature lovers.
aboutMandirText4: Surrounded by vast mountain ranges, deep valleys, flowing streams during monsoon, lush greenery, fragrant wildflowers, and winding trails, the journey to the temple is mesmerizing. A waterfall cascading from about 200 feet into the valley, chirping birds, and shy deer fleeing at human presence enhance the natural beauty. The fatigue of devotees disappears as they reach the temple atop the hill.
aboutMandirText5: From the northern gate, the Kanifnath temple can be seen. Looking down reveals the deep Garbhagiri valley, waterfalls, and dense greenery — a truly divine gift of nature. Amidst trees, mountains, valleys, and wildlife, Shri Sadguru Machindranath chose this place for eternal rest.
aboutMandirText6: In the tenth century Sadguru Machindranath on the Garbhagiri mountain top Samadhi took. The Samadhi is south-north and extremely vast. To the Samadhi sandalwood and Ashtagandha's coating applied is. On that shimmering embroidered saffron clothes are placed. Perfume, rose water sprinkling Champa flowers are offered. In front of the Samadhi holy, somewhat serious but pleasant atmosphere is. In front of the Samadhi itself Nath's Padukas (footprints) are. Daily early morning Kakada Aarti, afternoon 12 o'clock Naivedya Aarti and evening at this place lighting lamps Shejarti happens.
aboutMandirText7: At the time of Aarti thirty-three crore gods and goddesses at the main entrance gate standing are so it is believed. Devotees 'Bade Baba Shri Machindranath Maharaj ki Jai' in such name-chanting roar doing are. By mind and by honor greatest, than all gods also powerful and towards devotees merciful therefore to the Nath 'Bade Baba' called is. Also 'Mayamba' this also name is. In this name deep meaning filled is. 'May' means mother and 'Ba' means father. So parents just as their child's welfare see, love do, him protect, similarly Shri Machindranath also on devotees watch keeping are, their care take. Sadguru Shri Machindranath only devotees' true parents are. Therefore above name meaningful is. To him Sadguru Bade Baba, Mayamba, Kavi Narayan Machindranath, Maya Machindranath, Dada Guru Machindranath such many names are. Devotees him from heart love do and faith keep
aboutMandirText8: For centuries, this sacred Samadhi has radiated powerful spiritual energy, attracting millions of devotees from Maharashtra and beyond. It is not just a temple — it is a living spiritual legacy of the Nath tradition.
aboutMandirText9: From the sacred Machindranath Gad of Savaragaon to the broader Nath spiritual geography, Shri Machindranath Maharaj continues to inspire millions. This temple is not just a place of worship — it is a center of meditation, faith, fulfillment, and divine consciousness.

aboutMachindranathGadTitle: The Importance of Sacred Machindranath Gad (Mayamba) and Savaragaon Region
aboutMachindranathGadText1: Machindranath Gad (Mayamba) is an awakened (Jagrut) temple in Beed district. Here is the Sanjeevani Samadhi of Shri Machindranath. This Sanjeevan Samadhi temple, Shri Kshetra Machindranath Sanjeevani Samadhi Mandir (Mayamba), is located in District Beed, Maharashtra. Machindranath is one among the Navnath and is the first incarnation of Kavi Narayan. In the Nath tradition, Machindranath is considered an incarnation of Mahavishnu.
aboutMachindranathGadText2: In the same temple परिसर there is a pomegranate tree. Devotees come to that pomegranate tree and tie a thread (Navas) after making a vow and after the vow is fulfilled, they come again to untie the thread. To the left of the sanctum, there is a grand temple of Maruti. There are Audumbar trees in the परिसर. There is a beautiful idol of Nath seated on a horse. During the yatra, its musical procession is taken out.
aboutMachindranathGadText3: The entrance of Shri Machindranath Samadhi Temple and the Samadhi entrance of Shri Kanifnath Temple are in one straight line. It is said that both Nath go on horses to meet each other.
aboutMachindranathGadText4: In the Savaragaon area, apart from Shri Machindranath Sanjeevani Samadhi Temple, many more structures, things and temples can be seen.
aboutMachindranathGadText5: At the base of Nath Samadhi is Dhondai Devi. This goddess is considered the sister accepted by Nath. There is a tall rock like Amarnath Ling. Dhondai Devi is Goddess Lakshmi herself. Many devotees pray to the goddess and Nath and make vows. The goddess fulfills vows. Their wishes are fulfilled. After that, they offer traditional offerings (khana-naral). They feed married women and children. During the Shiv Yag Yagna of Vruddheshwar, Gorakshanath manifested ghee through Riddhi-Siddhi. That ghee was continuously flowing from the rock at this place. That ghee was used for Havan and food for Bhandara. Later for many days, lamps were lit on Machindranath Gad using this same ghee. There is such a legend. Nearby, from the cliff, a woman brought down a bullock cart as a vow. Sitting in the cart with her child, she descended into the valley risking her life. She had no children, so she made such a vow. After having a child, she fulfilled her vow. Because of her faith in Nath, she reached safely with the cart and bullocks.
aboutMachindranathGadText6: Nearby is the Dhuni temple. In it are beautiful idols of Shri Dattatreya and Shri Machindranath. Nath's items - Kamandalu, Trishul, Chimta, Jholi, Nath's photo are all kept in the Dhuni temple. In the Dhuni temple, the sacred fire burns continuously day and night. The Dhuni is used for meditation and fire worship. Devotees apply the sacred ash from this Dhuni on their foreheads. Devotees coming here meditate here. Due to the sanctity of the place and presence of Dhuni, happiness, peace and joy are obtained.
aboutMachindranathGadText7: Savji Baba was a dear devotee of Machindranath. He served Nath regularly for about 70 years. When he came to Machindranath Gad, there was dense forest. There were many wild animals. Still, he served Nath till death. He came at a young age to serve. He remained celibate for life and did cleaning, Aarti, Pooja, incense-lamp services. He lived alone in the temple for 70 years. He ask Bhiksha for survival. He gave shelter to travelers. His Samadhi is to the south of the temple. He died on Friday 26/4/1991.
aboutMachindranathGadText8: Near the Samadhi is the 'Nagarkhana'. During Aarti, the drum is played. Due to its loud sound, people in the area know that Aarti has started. Now an automatic mechanical drum is installed.
aboutMachindranathGadText9: On the path towards Savaragaon, there is a small pond. It is circular like a lake. One side has strong stone construction. This is the holy bath place of Machindranath. Devotees bathe here. Water from this pond is used for Pooja. There are many medicinal plants around. Washing clothes is strictly prohibited. It is believed that Nath and other deities bathe here every morning. Women are not allowed here.
aboutMachindranathGadText10: On the way to Devtalab, one comes across an ancient, large Champa tree; this location is also known as the 'Bhandarghar' (storehouse) of the Naths. On the first day of Paush Amavasya, all the villagers gather under this Champa tree to prepare 'Rot' using provisions collected from the village. They dig a pit in the ground, burn cow-dung cakes to create embers, place the prepared Rot inside, and then cover the pit with soil. By the next day, the Rot are roasted until they are perfectly crunchy. These are then offered as 'Naivedya' to the Nath deities. On the occasions of Rishi Panchami and Paush Amavasya, the 'Chhabina' (holy procession) of the Naths commences from this very spot and proceeds toward the Samadhi Temple.
aboutMachindranathGadText11: During the yatra, here a wrestling arena is filled. Wrestlers from far places come to play wrestling and mark their presence and go. Villagers give them rewards with great happiness. The enjoyment of this yatra is something different itself. As Machindranath is the revered deity of everyone, people from around four hundred to five hundred villages and devotees from urban areas — thus everyone gathers as one assembly. Everyone becomes absorbed in devotion.
aboutMachindranathGadText12: During the festival of Shri Machindranath, children (Bal-Gopals) are served meals in every household while chanting 'Narhari Pavanaganga.' This tradition is held in memory of the Samadhi festival. The source of this river lies to the east of Dhondai Devi, and it flows through the mountains. It is said that in ancient times, the river became sanctified by the bathing of all the deities and the dust from their feet during a Yajna (holy sacrifice), which is how it earned the name 'Pavanaganga.' This same Pavanagiri river flows through Shrikshetra Madhi and eventually merges with the Ganga Godavari. At the spot where the Pavanagiri waterfall cascades, there is a self-manifested (Swayambhu) Lingam of Amriteshwar and a Nandi. The holy water of the Pavana flows from a 'Gaumukh' (cow’s mouth) onto the Shiva Lingam. Devotees devoutly bathe the Lingam and the nearby idol of Lord Ganesha with this sacred water. Close by is the Ganesh Kund. At this site, some devotees sit for 'Parayana' (scriptural reading), while some sages engage in spiritual meditation. Some devotees even experience a divine vision of Amriteshwar in the form of a flame (Jyoti).
aboutMachindranathGadText13: One kilometer west of the Samadhi, nestled within the valley, lies a vast cave. The mountain has been carved in such a way that 400 to 500 people can easily sit inside at once. Due to the cave-temple style (Lenya) architecture, the deity residing here is known as 'Lenyai Devi.' Lord Gorakhnath established 'Satvai' here for the protection of this sacred place. Devotees offer prayers and fulfill their vows to ensure the well-being of their children and cattle; it is a common experience that she answers their prayers. This area is abundant with custard apple trees. Because of the flowing streams, dense greenery, and profound solitude, many great sages perform penance in this beautiful and tranquil spot. It was in this very cave that Gorakhnath taught Gahininath, and they were blessed by Adinath and other deities. This location is situated 2 km away from Machindranath Gad.
aboutMachindranathGadText14: After completing all pilgrimages of the three worlds, Shri Sadguru Machindranath performed a great yajna (bhandara) in Garbhagiri mountain. At that time at Vruddheshwar, chanters, ascetics, sanyasis of the earth, thirty-three crore deities, yaksha, gana, gandharva, sages, all rivers of the earth, all pilgrimages of the three worlds, riddhi-siddhi, navnidhi, and Kubera, along with Indra — all were invited. Everyone gathered there. Everyone was honored. In the presence of Adinath, a great bhandara took place. A great food donation happened. Everyone was satisfied. Clothes were distributed to all. Gahininath was given knowledge. For the welfare of the world, all gave blessings. At that time, the line of deities extended 8 km long. The place where this line reached is called Devarai. Later, at the foothill of Garbhagiri mountain near Ghatshiras, Adinath himself resided there in old form. Therefore, this place got the name Vruddheshwar (Mhatardev). This place is approximately 6 km from Machindranath Gad. There, a yajna of thirty-three crore deities had taken place.
aboutMachindranathGadText15: To the east of Vruddheshwar, at a distance of 6 km, on the Garbhagiri mountain, is the Sanjeevani Samadhi of Machindranath. Similarly, to the south of Machindranath, at a distance of 5 km, under a large banyan tree, there is a temple of Shani Dev. This temple is very ancient.

aboutMachindranathGadText21: Though Machindranath traveled across Nepal, Tibet, and South India, Savaragaon holds the highest importance as he chose this place for eternal meditation.
aboutMachindranathGadText22: Millions of devotees testify that visiting this place brings peace, fulfillment of wishes, mental balance, and divine blessings.
aboutMachindranathGadText23: Many years ago in Savargaon, there was a man who did not have a son. He made a vow to the Naths that if he were blessed with a son, he would offer a horse and lead a grand ceremonial procession through the entire village every year. Following this, he prepared a wooden idol of Machindranath seated on a horse and offered it to the deity. Later, the temple administration covered the idol with silver plating. Even today, this equestrian idol of the Nath can be seen in the 'Ghoda Mandir' located in front of the temple office within the Darshan queue building. This specific procession of the idol, accompanied by the holy 'Nishan' (flags), is known as the 'Chhabina.' During the Chhabina, the villagers bathe the idol, carry it reverently on their heads, and lead a vibrant procession with music and traditional fanfare.
aboutMachindranathGadText24: Opposite the Darshan queue building is the 'Navnath Temple,' where marble idols of all the nine Naths and Guru Dattatreya are enshrined. Right in front of it is a spacious hall where devotees perform 'Parayana' (ritualistic reading) of the 'Shri Navnath Bhaktisar,' 'Shri Gurucharitra,' and other sacred texts. As a result, one experiences a unique sense of serenity and divinity within this Parayana hall.

machindranathText1: According to the information given in Bhagavata, it is described that Rishabhadeva had a total of 100 sons, out of which nine were detached, and they are the nine Narayanas — Kavi, Hari, Antariksha, Prabuddha, Pippalayan, Avirhotra, Drumil, Chamas, and Karabhajan. In Kaliyuga, as per the command of Bhagavan Shri Krishna, they took birth again on Earth in the form of Navnath. Among them, the first son Kavi Narayan was born as 'Machindranath'. In the form of his disciple, Hari Narayan took incarnation as 'Gorakshanath'. Antariksha Narayan was born as 'Jalandharnath'. In the form of his disciple, Prabuddha Narayan incarnated as 'Kanifnath'. Pippalayan Narayan incarnated as 'Charpatnath'. Avirhotra Narayan incarnated as 'Vatsiddha Nagnath'. Drumil Narayan took birth as 'Bhartrinath'. Chamas Narayan incarnated as 'Revannath', and Karabhajan Narayan was born as 'Gahininath'.
machindranathText2: In the text 'Navnath Bhaktisar' written by Dhundisut Malu Narhari, the divine leelas of all the main Naths are narrated in verse form. Even today, the text 'Navnath Bhaktisar' is considered highly revered among Nathpanthis, in which the leelacharitra of Machindranath is described. While narrating the Nath leelas taken from the well-known text 'Goraksha Kimayagar', Dhundisut Malu Narhari explains the accounts of the nine incarnations of the nine Narayanas.
machindranathText3: At the beginning of Kaliyuga, Ramapati, Dwarakadheesh Shri Krishna called upon the Navayogeshwars, that is, the nine Narayanas. Shri Krishna instructed that Kavi, Hari, Antariksha, Narayan, Pippalayan, Avirhotra, Drumil, Chamas, and Karabhajan should now take incarnation in Kaliyuga. It was decided that Kavi Narayan should become Matsyendra and Hari Narayan should become Goraksha. 'Yavari bole Dwarakadheesh, Kavi Narayan jo ka pratyaksha, tene Machhindra houuni daksha, jagamaji miravaave' (1.38) — such was the command given by Krishna. A question arose as to where and how Kavi Narayan should take birth. At that time, from the veerya of Vidhi, that is Brahmadeva, eighty-eight thousand rishis were created, and some portions of that veerya were scattered in other places as well. One drop of that veerya had fallen into the waters of Yamuna river, which was swallowed by a fish. 'Tari prajnyik Kavi Narayan, tene matsyodari janma ghene, Machhindra aise jagant naamane miravaave Maharaja' (1.60).
machindranathText4: According to this plan, Machindranath was born. While Kavi Narayan was growing in the womb of the fish, on Kailasa, Aparna Mauli said to Shiva, 'Tumhi japata jo mantra, to maj dyava ji pavitra' (1.105). But for the proper transmission of this mantra, solitude was required. They found the desired solitude on the banks of Yamuna (1.109). In this solitude, the upadesha given by Shankara to Parvati was heard by Kavi Narayan in the womb of the fish — 'Aikale pari grahanachi jhale, tenekaroni jnan prakatle, meetu pan sarva sarale, sarvachi Brahma Sanatana' (1.93). This self-realized embryo came out in the form of an egg. The egg was broken by cranes, and from it emerged a radiant child. A fisherman named Kamik raised him. Kamik and his wife Sharadata lovingly took care of Machindra. When Machindra became five years old, he once went with Kamik to catch fish. Kamik was catching fish and putting them into a basket. Machindra could not bear the killing of his maternal lineage. He released all the fish back into the water. Kamik became angry at this act and said, 'Maase pakadaila kiti shram padtat! Sarv maase paanyat sodles, ata khanar kay?' To this, Matsyendra replied, 'Sarvant pavitra bhikshann, dosh tyas kahin nase' (1.165), and saying so, Machindra left from there with the intention of seeking alms.
machindranathText5: From Kashi kshetra, he went towards the north to Badrikashram. There he performed tapa for twelve years. Due to this tapascharya, his body became extremely thin. 'Tape bhakshile sakal maans, pari laag na laage asthitvaches… netra fironi jhalya vaati, dison laglya karpaas-riti… sarv anga gele valoni, kaashta pari miravatase' (1.172–74). While Machindra was absorbed in such tapascharya, Atisut Dattatreya appeared there. Shankara also arrived there. They saw the young ascetic Machindranath. What was his form like?
ovi1: जटा पिंगट नखें जळमट । कंटकारी पादांगुष्ठ । कार्पासमय झाली दृक् । त्वचा लिपटली अस्थींसी ॥ सर्वांगी शिरा ढळढळाट । दिसती अवनी नामपाठ । ध्वनिमात्र शब्द उठे । चलन-वलन नयनांचें ॥ (२.१०-११)
machindranathText6: On the instruction of Shankara, Dattatreya asked him the reason for his tapas. As soon as he recognized Dattatreya, Machindra was filled with great joy. Seeing his curiosity, Datta bestowed grace upon him and whispered a mantra into his ear. Machindra’s ignorance was removed, and he realized the supreme truth everywhere. When Shankara instructed that Machindra should be given knowledge of all siddhis and be fulfilled, Datta again imparted teachings to him. 'जें वेदकाणांचें निजसार । जें सर्वोपकारांचें गुहागार । सकळ सिद्धींचें अर्धमाहेर' — Machindra understood this from Datta. 'जारण मारण उच्चाटण । शापावपि निवारण । शरादपि अस्त्रादिनि बर्हण । मंत्रशक्ती त्या बरतल्या ॥... नागबकावि वातास्त्र । नगनगावि महावज्र । पावक जलधी अस्त्र पवित्र । सांगोपांग तो झाला ॥' (२.४७-५२). Dattatreya also taught him a yogamarga called Kanfadi. 'पुढील भविष्य जाणोनि । संप्रदाय केला निर्माण । षड्रूप जोगीदर्शन । कानफाडी मिरविले ॥ नाथ ऐसें देऊनि नाम । शिंगी शैली देऊन भूषण । ऐसें परिकरोनि प्रमाण । अभिनंदन पैं गेला ॥' (२.५४-५५).
machindranathText7: In this way, Machindra received sampradaya initiation from Adinath Shiva and Dattatreya, and he set out on pilgrimage. He offered salutations to Ambamata of Saptashrungi. In order to attain Shabari vidya in poetry, he performed anushthan before Amba for seven days. Pleased with him, Ambika then took Machindrasiddha to Martand mountain. There stood a Nagavriksha, the origin place of all siddhis. On its branches resided various gods and deities. Bavan Veer, Narasi, Kalika, Mahishasura, Mhasoba, Jhoting, Veerbhadra, Vetala, Maruti, Rama, Surya, Kumari, Dhanada, Nanda and others, along with Chanda, Chamunda, Rambha, Kuda, Jogini, Kalabhairava, Siddhabhairava, Shankhini, Dankhini, Yakshini and others resided on that tree. The Ashtasiddhis — Pratima, Kamya, Anima, Garima, Vashi, Swakarti, Prathima, Mahima — were also present there. Here, Machindranath performed japa of the Bijamantra. Amba also showed him the method to please these deities. She told him about a place of Mahakali on the bank of a river flowing south of Anjan mountain near Brahmagiri on Rishabha mountain. 'In this region there are one hundred white kundas filled with water. While going, one should place a white creeper in each kunda. In whichever kunda the creeper remains alive, one should bathe in it. After consuming the tirtha, slight unconsciousness will occur. In that state, one should chant the twelve Adityas. You will have darshan of Surya himself, and by his grace all the deities on the tree will come under your control.' Following this, through tirtha-sevan at Adityakunda, Machindra attained all knowledge from those tree-deities and received mantravidya. After that, Machindranath 'शाबरी विद्येचा ग्रंथ निर्मून । बंगालदेशीं चालता झाला ॥' (२.१०२).
machindranathText8: While continuing his pilgrimage, he reached Chandragiri village in the region called Bengal, situated on the shore of Helasamudra. There lived a Gaud Brahmin named Sarvopadyal, and his wife's name was Saraswati. Though devoted to rituals, japa, and tapa, they had no child. One day, chanting 'Alakh', Machindranath arrived in their courtyard. Saraswati welcomed him and shared her sorrow. Machindra took a pinch of bhasma from his bag, chanted the Surya mantra, and gave it to her. He blessed her that by consuming this bhasma she would be blessed with a son, and that he would return after twelve years to inquire. Saying this, Machindranath left on his journey. Saraswati told her friends and women around her about the incident. Then they said —
ovi2: अगे ऐसें सोंगें महीवरती । किती एक ठक ते बहु असती । नाना कवटाळें करून दाविती । जग भेविती जननीये ॥ आणि दुसरा त्यांत आहे अर्थ । कानफाटे कवटाळे व्यक्त । नाना परींच्या विद्या बहुत । तयांपासीं असती वो ॥ काय वो सांगूं शुभगामिनी । कानफाडे कृत्रिम मंत्रीं । जाया पाहून शुभगात्री । करिती कुत्रीं मंत्रानें ॥ मग ते तयांतें सर्व घेऊनी । हिंडती वस्ती क्षेत्रमेदिनीं । रात्रींमाजीं कांता करोनी । सुखशयनें भोगिती ते ॥ (२.१६२-६५)
machindranathText9: Hearing the words of her friends, Saraswati threw the bhasma into a heap of cow dung, and from that later Gorakshanath was born. Goraksha became the first renowned disciple of Matsyendra. Machindra continued his pilgrimage. At Setubandha of Rameshwar, he had darshan of Maruti, and a conflict arose between them leading to a display of siddhi-powered combat. In the end, Machindra bowed at the feet of Maruti and Vayu. Maruti advised him, 'You should go to the kingdom of women. There, the queen named Mainakini performed tapa to attain me. I gave her a boon that Machindra will fulfill your desire. Therefore, you should now go there.' Then —
ovi3: येरू म्हणे ऊर्ध्वरता । मातें कार्य हें निरोपितां । तरी ब्रह्मचर्यत्व समूळ वृक्षा । आचवलें जाईल ॥ मी तो उदास कामशक्ती । नोहे म्हणतील नाथपंधी । जती नामी जगविख्याती । जगामाजीं मिरवलों ॥ तरी ऐसी कुकर्मराहटी । मातें घडोनि येतां जेठी । मग वाग्देवता निंदा दिवशी । येऊून जगीं मिरवेल ॥ यापरी आणिक सिद्ध जगीं । नागपंथी आहेत योगी । तेही योगपंथ ते प्रसंगीं । विटाळ माझा करतील ॥ एवं स्त्रीसंग अभ्लाघ्य पर । अपकीतीचें दृढ भांडार । सर्वविनाशी मोहास्त्र । स्वीकारावें हें खोटेंना ॥ (२.११९-२३)
machindranathText10: Machindra did not initially accept the idea of staying in the kingdom of women, but finally Maruti said, 'बा रे योगभ्रमण । ही अनादि राहटी पूर्ण । भोग भोगितां निर्दोष' (२.१३१). He also said that Meeninaath would incarnate through him. Upon this, Machindra agreed and set out for darshan of Hingaladevi. There he had a great battle with the gatekeepers Ashtabhairava, where many miraculous weapons were used. Pleased by his powers, Ambika Hingaladevi granted him a boon. After receiving her blessing, Machindranath proceeded to Bara Malhar. In the forest of Bara Malhar, he fought with Vetala and his spirits, rendering them unconscious. Vetala, astonished by his power, ordered the spirits to assist Machindra. Then, after taking darshan of Kartikswami in Konkan, Machindra came to Adul village in Kudall region, where he fought with Kalikadevi and defeated her. By Shankara’s command, Kalikadevi then assisted him. At Hareshwar, after bathing at Gadatirtha and circumambulating the mountain, he met Veerbhadra, and a fierce battle took place. Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh calmed them. Veerbhadra accepted his greatness, and all the gods granted him various boons — Vishnu gave Chakrastra, Shankara gave Trishulastra, Brahmadeva gave Vaanisiddhi, Indra gave Vajrastra, Kubera gave Siddhimantra, Varuna gave Apastra, Agni gave Agnimantra, and Ashwini gave Mohinimantra.
machindranathText11: Machindranath had now attained all siddhis, and his pilgrimage continued. He took darshan of Vajrabhagavati at Vajrabhavan located west of Kevadadesh. Establishing Bhogavati Kunda, he went to Itakanath. At Ayodhya, he bathed in the Sarayu river and had darshan of Rama. At that time, a Pashupata king was ruling. Here also, Machindra performed many miracles and facilitated the meeting of Ramachandra and Pashupata.
ovi4: असो आतां येथूनि मच्छिंद्रनाथ ॥ सप्त मोक्षपुर्‍य पाहूनि त्वरित ॥ अयोघ्या मथुरा अवंतिका यथार्थ ॥ काशी काश्मिरी पाहिलीं ॥६॥ मिथिला प्रयाग गया सुग्ग ॥ तेथें नमूनि विष्णुपदास ॥ अन्य तीर्थे करुनि बंगालदेश ॥ चंद्रागिरीस तो पातला ॥७॥
machindranathText12: While asking for alms in the village, Machindranath saw a Brahmin's house and remembered that earlier he had given mantra-siddha sacred ash to a woman named Saraswati for the attainment of a son. He called out to her. Saraswati came outside and gave alms. After recognizing her, he asked about the son, but she said that she had not yet been blessed with a son. Hearing this, Machindranath asked her what happened to the ash that was given. Then she became frightened and admitted that she had thrown it on the garbage heap. She asked for forgiveness. Machindranath, without becoming angry, told her to show that place. She took him near the heap of cow dung. Then he addressed that heap and called out.
ovi5: हे हरीनारायण प्रतापवंता ॥ मित्रवर्या सूर्यसुता ॥ जरी असशील या गोवरांत ॥ नीघ त्वरित या समयीं ॥७२॥ या गोवरगिरींत नरदेहजन्म ॥ मिरवला असें तूतें उत्तम ॥ तरी गोरक्ष ऐसें तूतें नाम ॥ सुढाळपणीं मज वाटे ॥७३॥
gorakshanathText1: From inside, a voice came saying, “I am Gorakshanath, but I cannot come outside.” Then the heap was moved aside and he was brought out. That radiant child came out. Seeing this, Saraswati felt great repentance. But Machindranath said that the child was not in her destiny. Afterwards, Gorakshanath bowed at his feet. Machindranath gave him initiation and, taking him along, set out for pilgrimage.
gorakshanathText2: Machindranath, taking Gorakshanath along, while performing pilgrimage, came to the village of Kanakgiri. There, being troubled by hunger, he sent Gorakshanath for alms. Gorakshanath went to a Brahmin's house. On that day, due to the ancestral ritual, many prepared dishes were ready. The housewife, seeing his radiant face, was impressed and gave him plenty of food. He returned to the Guru and offered the alms. Machindranath accepted that food with love, but the desire for vada remained. He told Gorakshanath to bring more vada. Gorakshanath again went to that house and began to ask for vada. The housewife said, why do you not say directly that you want them? To that Gorakshanath said that this is for the Guru’s wish. To test him, she asked him for one eye. Without even a moment of delay, Gorakshanath removed his own eye and placed it before her. Seeing this, she became frightened and, with repentance, began to ask forgiveness while giving him vada. Gorakshanath explained to her and, taking the eyeball, returned to the Guru. When the Guru saw the bandage, he asked, then Gorakshanath at first avoided, but upon insistence, told the entire incident. Then Machindranath, by mantra power, restored his eye to its original state. Afterwards, both took food. Staying there for some time, Machindranath taught him Sabari Vidya and Astra Vidya and placed him at the feet of all deities. He made him have the darshan of Narsi, Kalika, Mhanda, Mhaisur, Zoting Vetala, Maruti, Shri Ram and others. When the meeting with Ram happened, Ram seated Gorakshanath on his lap and gave blessings. Thus, along with the fifty-two Veers, Shri Ram, Surya and others, all gave boons to Goraksha and instructed Machindranath to make him sit for penance, and they all returned to their respective places.
gorakshanathText3: One day, Gorakshanath was sitting chanting the Sanjeevani mantra. At that time, Machindranath was not nearby. Meanwhile, some children came near him while playing. They were making a cart with mud. They asked Gorakshanath to make a figure of a cart driver. He agreed and began to make a figure of mud. According to prior indication, in that figure, the incarnation of Karbhajan among the Navnarayanas was to manifest. As Gorakshanath completed the figure while chanting the mantra, life entered into it and it became a living child and began to cry. Seeing this, the children got frightened and ran away. Later, the villagers came to know this incident. Everyone was astonished that a mud figure became alive. The fame of Machindranath’s yogic power spread.
gorakshanathText4: Machindranath was thinking of taking that child along, but the villagers said that without a mother, his upbringing would not be possible. Then it was decided to give the responsibility of the child to Madhunabha Brahmin and his devoted wife Ganga. They had no children, so it was believed that they would raise him well. Machindranath placed that child in the lap of Gangabai and said that this is the incarnation of Karbhajan. His name should be kept as Gahininath. In the future, he will become great and will bless a yogi named Nivrutti. By mantra power, milk was produced in Gangabai’s breasts. She lovingly began to raise the child and named him Gahininath.
gorakshanathText5: After some days, traveling with Goraksha through many pilgrimages, Machindranath came to Badrikashram. There he prayed to Shankar and made Goraksha sit for penance, and himself again set out on pilgrimage. As previously promised to Maruti, Machindranath began to live in the Stri-rajya at a place called Shrungmarud along with Tilottama and a queen named Mainakini. The queen of Stri-rajya, Mainakini, and Machindranath were enjoying all kinds of pleasures. They also had a son. His name was kept as Meennath.
jalindarNathText1: In the Kuru lineage, in the seventh generation of King Janamejaya, King Brihadrava was born. He was ruling over Hastinapur. Once he started a great Somayajna. At that time, earlier, from the eye of Shankar, the fire of destruction had burned Madan, and that fire was growing in the womb of Agni. In that fire, Antariksha Narayan entered, and that embryo was placed into the sacrificial fire pit. After the completion of the yajna, when the Brahmins were putting their hands into the pit to remove the ashes, they found a boy. This wonderful incident was told by the priest to the king. King Brihadrava saw that child and became extremely happy. He lovingly lifted the child and began to pamper him. He felt as if Madan himself had incarnated. The king immediately took that child into the inner palace to Queen Surachana. The queen was extremely beautiful and divine in form, as if Lakshmi, Saraswati or Parvati herself had incarnated. The queen asked, “Whose child is this?” Then the king said that “This is the blessing of Agni Narayan. He will assist our son named Meenket.” Hearing this, the queen lovingly took that child. As soon as she placed him near her breast, milk began to flow from her breasts. Therefore, a great celebration was held in the palace. On the twelfth day, that child was placed in the cradle and his name was kept as Jalandar. On that day, sugar was distributed throughout the village and charity was given to the poor.
jalindarNathText2: Later, King Brihadrava performed the thread ceremony (Upanayana) of Jalandhar. After some time, the thought of his marriage occurred to the King. For this, he sent Minister Dhumin and the priest together to find a suitable bride. When Minister Dhumin and the priest did not return for several days, Jalandhar one day asked his mother, “Where has the Minister gone?” She replied, “Your father has sent them to find a wife for you.” Hearing this, Jalandhar asked, “What is a wife?” To this, his mother replied, “A woman like me is a wife.” This thought remained in his mind. Later, when he went to play, he asked his friends, “My parents are going to get me married, but what is a wife for?” His friends then told him about the true nature of worldly life. Hearing this, a sense of detachment (Vairagya) arose in Jalandhar's mind. He thought, “This world is base, and one should stay away from such things.” With this resolve, he went alone into the forest. The guards at the village border saw him, but being a prince, they did not question him. However, they informed the King. Terrified, the King set out to find him personally. Many people were searching, but Jalandhar could not be found. Finally, everyone returned disappointed. The King and Queen were deeply grieved by his separation.
jalindarNathText3: Meanwhile, while Jalandhar was sleeping in the forest, a wildfire broke out at night. The fire approached him, but the fire recognized him. Agni (the Fire God) protected him and moved him to a safe place. Then Agni appeared personally, woke Jalandhar, and sat him on his lap. Jalandhar asked, “Who are you?” Agni replied, “I am your parent.” Jalandhar was surprised, so Agni told him the entire story of his birth. Hearing this, Jalandhar said, “Since I have received this human birth, it must achieve something great. Let my fame remain in the three worlds and let me become immortal.” Seeing his firm resolve, Agni was delighted. Then Agni took him to Dattatreya. He accepted Jalandhar with respect. Agni told the whole story and requested, “Take him under your shelter and make him great.” Dattatreya said, “He will have to stay here for twelve years.” Agni agreed. Dattatreya sat Jalandhar on his lap, destroyed his ignorance, and gave him knowledge. After that, Agni vanished. Following this, Jalandhar began living with Dattatreya. He would bathe in the Bhagirathi every day and seek the blessings of Vishveshvara. Later, he would beg for alms in Kolhapur and take his meals at Panchaleshvara.
jalindarNathText4: In this way, by staying in the company of Dattatreya for twelve years, Jalandhar became proficient in all weaponry, Vedas, scriptures, Puranas, and grammar, becoming a great Siddha. Having become perfect in this manner, Dattatreya worshipped all the deities. Pleased by that worship, all the gods appeared to grant boons to Jalandhar. At that time, Agni Dev also arrived and was overjoyed to see Jalandhar skilled in all sciences. Then Dattatreya said to Agni Dev, “Now he is proficient in all knowledge. Now the deities should be pleased and brought before him so he can receive boons from them.” Hearing this, Agni Dev sat Jalandhar on his shoulders and showed him all the deities of the three worlds. The same deities from whom Machindranath had previously obtained boons after pleasing them also granted boons to Jalandhar. Thereafter, Jalandhar went to Badrikashram and performed severe penance there for twelve years. When the test of that penance was completed, all the deities nodded in satisfaction. Following that, Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh, and all other deities blessed him, and they all returned to their respective abodes satisfied.
jalindarNathText5: Later at Badrikashram, Badrinath (Shankar) kept Agni and Jalandarnath near himself for three nights. At that time, a contrary event that had occurred in Satyalok was told by Shankar, which is as follows — when Brahmadeva's daughter Saraswati was twelve years old, seeing her form and the neatness of her limbs, Brahmadeva became afflicted with desire. Then he was driven towards indiscretion. As he followed behind her, while running, his semen was discharged. Then by the force of the wind, that drop of semen went and fell into the ear of an elephant in the forest of Himachal. At that place, PrabuddhaNarayan entered. After this event happened, ages upon ages passed, yet that elephant remained alive. From its ear, the incarnation-birth of PrabuddhaNarayan was to take place. Jalandar should make him his disciple. Since he was born from the ear, his name would be ‘Kanifa’ — thus Shankar said.
ovi6: In the eight directions there are eight diggajas ॥ greatly radiant are those great beings ॥ among them one is a mass of brilliance ॥ that great one is situated ॥84॥ Prabuddha Narayan is renowned ॥ the initiation of incarnation is established in the body ॥ in the ear cavity of that diggaja ॥ he is beautifully present ॥85॥ his body is like the rays of the young sun ॥ he should be seen with one's own eyes ॥ making him a disciple Jalandar ॥ should make him renowned on earth ॥86॥ his emergence is from the ear ॥ therefore his name is Kanifa ॥ hearing such words of Shiva ॥ Vaishvanara speaks ॥87॥
jalindarNathText6: Hearing this, Agni said, “You are telling a very wondrous matter; but where that elephant is, that should be shown. If that happens, my son will receive a great support.” After Agni made such a request, Shankar took Jalandar and Agni to the forest of the Himalayas to show the location of that elephant. There, upon a mountain, a विशाल and mountain-like powerful elephant was seen. Then Shankar said, “This elephant is extremely powerful. What method should be used to bring it under control?” Then Jalandar replied with courage, “O Maharaj! Upon my head is the boon-giving hand of Dattatreya. Its effect you will now see. If even the time of Pralay can be stopped before it, then what of this elephant?” Saying this, he took a pinch of bhasma from his bag, chanted the mantra of Mohiniastra, and after मंत्रित the Sparshastra, he threw that bhasma upon the elephant. At that moment, that powerful elephant became completely calm. Then Jalandar alone went near the elephant. He lovingly addressed the elephant, “There is none as courageous as you. In your ear, a divine jewel has been formed. O capable PrabuddhaNarayan! You have taken birth in the ear of the elephant, therefore your name has been given ‘Kanifa’. Now you come out quickly.”
ovi7: Calling out he spoke to him ॥ he says O capable Prabuddha Narayan ॥ becoming manifest in the elephant’s ear ॥ you are displaying the initiation of incarnation ॥11॥ therefore now immediately ॥ leaving the ear come outside ॥ your name according to this body ॥ Karnakanifa is befitting ॥12॥ from Brahmaveerya the ear-birth has happened ॥ therefore this name is given to you ॥ you indeed are Kanifa the all-knowing form ॥ why do you not become visible ॥13॥
jalindarNathText7: Hearing Jalandhar’s words, Kanifa said, “O King, treasure of virtues! Please remain steady.” Then he came out from the elephant’s ear. At that time, the radiant form of a sixteen-year-old was supported by Jalandhar with his own hands and brought down to the ground. After that, seating him on his shoulder, Jalandhar took him to Shankar and told him to get down and bow to Shankar and Agni. Hearing this, Kanifa bowed to Shankar and Jalandhar. Then Shankar lovingly seated him on his lap and kissed him. Further, to grant him grace, Jalandhar requested Shankar. Thinking that without grace ignorance would not be destroyed, and remembering the Guru as instructed by Shankar, Jalandharnath placed his hand on Kanifa’s head and imparted the mantra into his ear. By that initiation, his ignorance was immediately destroyed. Then all four went to Badrikashram. At that time, Dattatreya told Jalandhar, “Whatever I have given you, give all of it to Kanifa.” Saying this, Agnidev disappeared.
jalindarNathText8: There Shankar continued to meet them for six months. In those six months, Kanifa became proficient in all knowledge. However, Jalandhar had not taught him the two weapons Sanjeevani and Vatakarsan. In order that Kanifa should receive weapon knowledge and the grace of the deities, Shankar told Jalandhar. Then Jalandhar folded his hands and prayed — “Kanifa has become proficient in all knowledge; he should be granted boons.” Hearing this, all the deities said, “We granted you boons because Dattatreya taught you knowledge and Agni also blessed you. Respecting their word, we gave you boons; but we cannot grant such boons repeatedly. In the future you will have countless disciples; how can we grant boons to each?” Saying this, the gods began to depart in their aerial vehicles. Seeing this, Jalandharnath became extremely angry. He said, “Disrespecting me you are leaving; but you have not yet seen my power. Now I will show you my miracle.” Saying this, he used the Vata weapon. A tremendous wind arose and the gods’ vehicles began to scatter. Then the deities released their weapons; but Jalandhar rendered them ineffective. Hari and Hara were watching this miracle from afar. Seeing their weapons fail before Jalandharnath, the gods decided to descend with weapons. First they thought to take Agni’s life and descended to the earth. At that time Jalandhar released the Kamini weapon. From it thousands of beautiful women were created. Then he activated the Kama weapon. Because of this, the gods became lustful and began to run after those women. The women ran ahead and the gods followed them pleading. In this way, all entered a forest of berry trees. The women climbed the trees, and the gods also climbed after them. At that moment, Jalandhar cast sacred ash with the Sparsha weapon mantra. As a result, the gods’ feet stuck to the trees. Some gods hung upside down — head downward and feet upward. Then Hari and Hara also appeared there and said, “Today a remarkable sight has been seen!” At that moment those women removed all the gods’ garments and made them naked. All those garments were brought and piled near Jalandharnath.
jalindarNathText9: Then Jalandharnath signaled and showed this condition to Kanifa. After that, Kanifa began to clothe each god one by one. Seeing their miserable condition, the gods felt great remorse. Then Kanifa said, “I am giving you clothes without the knowledge of my Guru; but do not tell this to my Guru.” He gave each god garments and bowed at their feet. Seeing this humble devotion of Kanifa, the gods became pleased. They happily granted him boons and promised that in weapon knowledge they would remain favorable to him in every way. Then Jalandharnath released the separating weapon. As a result, all the gods stuck to the trees were freed. They again wore their weapons and ornaments and came near Jalandharnath and bowed to him. They said, “We will manifest ourselves in the form of weapons and grant you realization.” Then Jalandharnath said, “I will compose Sabari poetry in the future; for that, all of you please assist.” The deities agreed and gave their word and all returned to their respective abodes.
jalindarNathText10: Further, Shankar and Vishnu went to Badrikashram along with Jalindarnath and Kanifnath. They all were stunned after seeing the power of Jalindarnath. While their mutual conversations were ongoing, seeing the defiance of the deities done by Jalindar, they began to praise him. They also remarked that until today, no one so capable had been found who could challenge the deities. Later, Shankar told Jalindar, “You go to the place of Nagpatra-Ashwattha, perform a Yagya, and there, by creating poetry, obtain boons from the deities. The mantras of Vedic knowledge are many, and the science of weapons is great and influential; but its brilliance will not endure in the Kali Yuga. Even the knowledge of mantras will not be of much use to the people. Therefore, you establish and perfect the poetic compositions. And teach all those sciences to Kanifnath. This Kanifnath is generous by nature; even if there is a little hypocrisy in him, he will still be useful at the right time. He will make thousands of disciples and will become proficient in all sciences. Because of this, his dominance will remain throughout the entire world.”
jalindarNathText11: Previously, Sabari Rishi had discovered the path of mantra-vidya; but because that knowledge was limited, people did not benefit much from it. Therefore, it is necessary to prepare one hundred crore poems, and that task should be performed by the Navnaths. All this practice is to be done only for the welfare of others. You are omniscient; there is no need to tell you this. Poems should also be composed on Jaran, Maran, Ucchatan, etc.” Thus Shankar told Jalindarnath. Also, regarding Kanifnath, he said, “Make him sit for penance and make him capable.” Jalindarnath accepted all these words of Shankar. After that, Jalindar and Kanifnath stayed there for twelve years and created forty crore twenty lakh poems. Seeing that, Shankar was pleased. Then he went under the Nag Ashwattha and guided them to achieve the perfection of those experiments. Accordingly, both of them went there. They performed Havan there and perfected the experiments. Bringing holy water from the Suryakunda, they sprinkled it on the fifty-two Veers and obtained their favor. After this, they returned to Badrikashram again. There, Jalindarnath made Kanifnath sit for penance and also engaged himself in penance. Gorakshanath was also performing penance at that same place; however, they had no information about each other.
jalindarNathText12: Meanwhile, Jalindarnath was wandering on a pilgrimage. He used to carry a bundle of grass on his head, go from the forest to the village, and feed it to the cows there. So that he would not feel the weight and suffer distress from having the bundle on his head, the Wind would hold that bundle mid-air at some distance above his head. In this manner, carrying the bundle of grass above his head, Jalindarnath, while wandering, reached Helapattan in the Gauda-Bengal country. Then, the people there began to feel great wonder as to how the bundle of grass remained above the head without any support. Thinking that he was some Siddha Purusha, they began to go for his Darshan. He lived in a dirty place in the village and managed his livelihood by begging for alms. King Gopichand, the son of King Trilochan, was the king there at that time. King Gopichand's mother, Mainavati, was a very virtuous woman. One day, while she was watching the beautiful view of the city from the balcony of the royal palace, she saw Jalindarnath. Seeing such a Yogi carrying a bundle of grass above his head without support, she was astonished. It came to her mind that some glorious personage had descended upon the earth. Then, she resolved that she should make him her Guru and make her life meaningful. She called her maidservant. That maidservant was clever. As soon as she arrived, she stood with folded hands.
jalindarNathText13: Mainavati said to her, “I have a very delicate task. This matter must not leak out. Depending on the situation, it could cost a life, so be careful. Find out secretly where that Yogi is going.” The maid was amazed upon seeing Jalindarnath. She told Mainavati, “We should go and take his grace and become free from the cycle of birth and death.” The maid followed Jalindarnath. In the evening, he sat peacefully in a dirty place. Seeing that place, the maid returned and informed Mainavati. Then Mainavati took fruits and delicacies in a plate. At midnight, she went to Jalindarnath along with the maid.
jalindarNathText14: He was sitting in meditation. Both of them fell at his feet and stood with folded hands. Mainavati praised him greatly. To test her, Jalindarnath started harassing her—he would throw stones at her and hurl abuses. But Mainavati’s courage did not waver; she kept requesting continuously. She was sure that “even if death comes by his hand, I will attain salvation.” Finally, Jalindarnath asked, “Who are you? Why have you come here?” She said, “O King of Yogis! I am the wife of the great and powerful King Trilochan. But because he has died, I am drowned in the sorrow of widowhood. Seeing this cycle of birth and death makes me afraid. Please release me from the fear of the God of Death.” He said, “The noose of Death is very difficult. It will not be broken by a ghost-like being like me. You go to your home. If your son comes to know of this, a disaster will occur.” At dawn, she bowed and went home. She felt no peace all day; again at night, she went with the maid. She started pressing his feet and would return in the morning after bowing. In this way, she performed uninterrupted service for six months. One day, Jalindarnath took a severe test of her. He created an illusory bumblebee and pretended to sleep. That bumblebee entered under her thigh and tore her thigh, making it bloody. Even then, Mainavati did not move. Her courage remained unshakable. Seeing her firm determination, Jalindarnath was pleased. He gave her the initiation of the mantra, and her complexion became divine. Placing her head on his feet, she said, “Today my birth has become meaningful.” Later, Jalindarnath inspired the Sanjivani mantra into her body. Because of this, Mainavati became immortal. Just as Ramchandra made Vibhishana immortal, in the same way, Jalindarnath made Mainavati immortal.
jalindarNathText15: After taking the advice of Jalindarnath, the joy Mainavati felt was beyond containment, and she felt that her coming into this birth had become meaningful. However, she also felt supreme grief because just as her husband Trilochan's body was turned to ashes in the crematorium, her son Gopichand's would also be. Therefore, she was waiting for an opportunity for many days to tell her son two words of wisdom.
jalindarNathText16: On a day in the month of Magh, Mainavati was sitting in the sun on the terrace of the palace to ward off the cold. At that same opportunity, King Gopichand was sitting below on a sandal-wood square stool studded with jewels, having fragrant oils and perfumes applied to his body by women. Other beautiful women were also around him. While the king was about to take a bath in such great luxury, Mainavati, up above, felt bad thinking that this beautiful body of Gopichand would perish. At that time, a surge of sorrow came over her and she burst into tears, which could not be controlled by any means. When those tears of hers fell on the king's body, the king was startled and began to look here and there, wondering where the warm water had fallen from. Then he saw that his mother was sitting and crying on the upper floor. At that time the king was rinsing his mouth and brushing his teeth; he got up just like that and went to his mother, and stood with folded hands after falling at her feet. Then he said, “Mother! Please tell me quickly what is the reason for your crying. Tell me who has troubled you. At this moment I will gouge out his eyes! If I do not alleviate your sorrow, then my birth from your womb is in vain. I will do anything for the satisfaction of your mind. While doing that, even if it costs my life, I will not rest without removing your sorrow.” Hearing this speech of King Gopichand, Mainavati said, “Being the mother of such a great and powerful King Gopichand, who is there to trouble me? But the only reason for my sorrow is that your father was as handsome as you; but after being seized by Time, his body turned to ashes in an instant. I feel very bad because your form is destined for the same fate. Instead of letting the body turn to waste in the soil, I see this path as best: to plan a strategy to be released from the time of Death. One should achieve as much of one's own welfare as possible. Gopichand, do not be deceived by fleeting luxury and make your life meaningful; but looking at your current attitude, I feel pity for you, and for this reason alone, I cried. Otherwise, I have not been insulted by anyone.”
jalindarNathText17: Then the king said, “Mother! Your saying is true. But where can I find such a Guru nowadays? Firstly, if he himself is immortal, then he will make me immortal. So who is such a person these days?” Then Mainavati said, “Child! Jalindarnath is of that same caliber and he has currently come to our city. Therefore, you surrender to him in body, speech, and mind, and without holding greed for this perishable luxury, get your body made immortal by him.” Hearing this, Gopichand said, “By his advice, I will be separated from my wife and children, happiness and wealth, royal glory and everything else! For this reason, I will not be able to take up Yoga suddenly today. Let me enjoy all kinds of pleasures for another twelve years. Then I will surrender to the Guru and accept the path of Yoga.” Then the mother said, “Son, one cannot give a guarantee of even a single moment for this body. Such being the case, you take the risk of twelve years! Child, who has seen twelve years? It cannot be said what situation may arise at what time.” Lumavati (the chief queen) was hiding and listening to this advice of Mainavati. Hearing it, she felt supreme sorrow. She said in her mind, “This is not a mother, but an enemy. This mother-in-law, who tells the king to leave his luxury, is not a mother-in-law but a sorceress.” She went to her palace and started thinking. Gopichand, after comforting his mother, went to take a bath.
jalindarNathText18: इधर लुमावती ने अपनी सौतों को बुलाया। उन्हें मैनावती की योजना बताई, “गोपीचंद को जोगी बनाकर राज्य नष्ट करने का उसका इरादा है। जालंदर नाम का पाखंडी गाँव में आया है। उसके प्रभाव से राजा बदल रहा है।” उसने आगे योजना रखी, “राजा के मन में संदेह पैदा करना चाहिए। जालंदर और मैनावती पर आरोप लगाना चाहिए। राजा क्रोधित होकर उसका विनाश कर देगा।” सभी स्त्रियों को यह योजना जंच गई। उस रात राजा लुमावती के महल में गया। उसने प्रेम से उससे बात करके उसका विश्वास जीत लिया। फिर वह बोली, “मेरे सुनने में एक बात आई है। पर बताने में डर लगता है।” राजा द्वारा अभय देने पर उसने बताया, “जालंदर यह वैरागी मैनावती के वश में हो गया है। दोनों मिलकर आपको जोगी बनाकर राज्य हड़पने का विचार कर रहे हैं।” यह सुनकर राजा को अत्यंत क्रोध आया। उसने तुरंत जालंदरनाथ को पकड़ कर लाने की आज्ञा दी। एक बड़ा गड्ढा खोदकर उसमें जालंदरनाथ को डाल दिया, उस पर घोड़ों की लीद डालकर गड्ढा भर दिया। और सख्त चेतावनी दी, “यह बात किसी को बताई तो प्राण ले लूँगा।” डर के मारे कोई कुछ नहीं बोला; रात में ही यह कार्य होने के कारण गाँव को भी पता नहीं चला। अगले दिन खबर फैली, “जालंदरनाथ चले गए।” यह समाचार सुनकर मैनावती को बहुत दुःख हुआ; उसकी बनाई योजना विफल हो गई। पर राजा आनंदित हुआ; ग्रामीणों को उस साधु के दर्शन मिलना बंद हो गए।
ovi8: असो गर्तेमाजी यतिनाथ ॥ वज्रासनातें घालोनि खालतें ॥ आकाशास्त्र प्रेरुनि भोंवतें ॥ स्वस्थचित्तीं बैसला ॥९३॥ आकाशास्त्र असतां भोंवतें ॥ लीद मिरवे सभोंवतें ॥ यापरी आकाशास्त्र माथां ॥ वज्रास्त्र स्थापिलें ॥९४॥ तेणेंकरोनि अधरस्थळी ॥ लीद मिरविली आहे शिरीं ॥ येरीकडे अंतःपुरीं ॥ जनवार्ता समजली ॥९५॥
gorakshanathText6: Gorakshanath and Kanifnath performed penance in Badrikashram for twelve years. After that, both of them set out in search of their Guru; but because the Guru was not found, they became extremely anxious. Kanifnath went to the kingdom of women (Strirajya). There, Machindranath was in royal pleasure with Queen Mainakini. As soon as he learned of Kanifnath's arrival, Machindranath felt that Gorakshanath would come to take him back, therefore he kept Kanifnath with great respect and tried to involve him in sensual pleasures; but Kanifnath and his disciples did not fall prey to it. Finally, Machindranath saw him off with great honor.
gorakshanathText7: While Gorakshanath was traveling on a pilgrimage from Jagannath, he met Kanifnath in the forest. Both honored each other by saying “Aadesh.” Kanifnath seated Gorakshanath on a brocade carpet. A thought came to Kanifnath's mind to test Gorakshanath's knowledge. He mentioned the ripe fruits on the mango tree in front and expressed a desire to bring them. Gorakshanath said that, instead of depending on disciples, one should bring fruits by one's own yogic power. Accepting this, Kanifnath threw sacred ash with mantra power and brought all the mangoes down from the tree. Everyone ate those fruits. After this, to show his own miracle, Gorakshanath manifested various fruits with mantra power. Everyone ate those too. Then Gorakshanath brought up the matter of sticking the remaining fruits back onto the tree. Kanifnath said that it was impossible, Gorakshanath said, “Nothing is difficult for an absolute devotee of the Guru. He will even create another Brahma. I will do whatever I wish by the grace of my Sadguru.” Hearing this, Kanifnath said in anger,
ovi9: म्हणे हो हो जाणतों तूतें ॥ आणि तुझिया गुरुसहित ॥ बहुसाधनीं प्रतापवंत ॥ नरकामाजी पचतसे ॥७७॥ वाचे म्हणविती योगीजन ॥ कर्म आचरती नरकपतन ॥ सकळ स्त्रीराष्ट्र वेष्टून ॥ भोग पापांचा ॥७८॥ जितेंद्रियत्व दावावें जनीं ॥ असोनि भोग चिंती मनी ॥ तया भोगवश करोनि ॥ मेनिकानाथ होवोनि ठेला ॥७९॥ तरी ठाऊक गुरु तुझा ॥ किती बोलसी प्राज्ञी ओजा ॥ आतां ब्रह्मयातें करुनि हीन तेजा ॥ ढिसाळ गोष्टी करितोसी ॥८०॥ प्रथम गुरु तुझा काबाडी ॥ तुझी दैना कोण फेडी ॥ आतां सोडोनि सकळ प्रौढी ॥ मार्गालागी क्रमी कां ॥८१॥
ovi10: तुझा गुरु जालिंदरनाथ ॥ प्रतापहीन दीन बहुत ॥ दशवर्षे आजपर्यंत ॥ नरकीं नित्य पचतसे ॥८३॥ परी त्या सामर्थ्य नाहीं झालें ॥ कीं आपण येथूनi जावें वहिलें ॥ नृपसर्पदपें वेष्टिलें ॥ शक्तिहीन झालासे ॥८४॥ हेळापट्टणीं गौडबंगाल देशीं ॥ वस्ताद मिळाला आहे त्यासी ॥ धन्य गोपीचंद प्रतापराशी ॥ लीदगर्तीत पचवीतसे ॥८५॥ तैसा नोहे गुरु माझा ॥ हालवील सकळ ब्रह्मांड चोजा ॥ शंकराचें अस्त्र ओजा ॥ करकमळीं मिरवतसे ॥८६॥ अष्टभैरव महादारुण ॥ अजिंक्य देवांदानवांकारण ॥ त्यांसी बळें करुनि कंदन ॥ शरणागत आणिलें ॥८७॥ पाहे केवढा मारुतसुत ॥ जेणें विजयी केला रघुनाथ ॥ तया मस्तकीं देऊनि पर्वत ॥ उभा केला स्तंभापरी ॥८८॥ वीरभद्र प्रतापतरणी ॥ देवदानवां अजिंक्य करणी ॥ तयाचा प्राण कंठीं आणुनी ॥ शरणागत तो केला ॥८९॥ द्वादशकळी तीव्र आदित्य ॥ तयाचा उलथोनि पाडिला रथ ॥ सकळ देव शरणागत ॥ होऊनि लोटले पायासी ॥९०॥ तरी प्रतापी गुरु ऐसा ॥ भक्त सोडवीत नरकक्लेशा ॥ तयाच्य वरदकृपें ऐसा ॥ आतांचि पाहें हे भ्रष्टा ॥९१॥
gorakshanathText9: Saying this, he threw sacred ash with the Sanjivani mantra, and the remaining fruits went and hung back on the tree. Seeing this, Kanifnath was amazed. He said humbly, “Today I have gained a great benefit—the whereabouts of my Guru have been found.” Gorakshanath said, “Just as you found your Guru, I too have found the search for my Guru Machindranath. Today's union has been excellent.” Both bowed to each other. Then Gorakshanath set out towards the kingdom of women and Kanifnath towards Helapattan.
kanifanathText1: The moment the news was received that his Guru Jalindarnath had been buried by King Gopichand, the fire of anger arose in Kanifa's mind and he felt an urge as to when he would take revenge. He came and stayed in the forest of Helapattan with his seven hundred disciples. As soon as the news of Kanifa's arrival was received, King Gopichand decided to go and meet him. He had already heard of Kanifa's reputation, therefore it had filled the King's mind to make him his Guru from the heart. Carrying with himself elephants, horses, camels, palanquins, carts, tents, camps, small tents etc., Kanifnath was touring the country with great glory along with seven hundred disciples. While the King was going with great pomp with his seven hundred commanders and countless army to bring Kanifa into the city, on the way he said to the minister “By the connection of destiny, the feet of a great Siddha Purusha have touched this city today. In that sense, it has come to my mind that he should be made a Guru. This Guru is suitable for me and his glory is also like my glory. Otherwise, the Guru whom our mother made was absolutely destitute and dirty. I am a King; only royal people are suitable to sit in my row. My mother made that Jalindar a Guru who wanders like a ghost, stays in a dirty place and is poor. But whatever thing is to be done, it should be done only after considering the pros and cons. To make a Guru for a King like me, he must be wealthy like this. This Kanifa I have found to be a suitable Guru.” Speaking thus, the King went with great ceremony to bring Kanifa.
kanifanathText2: The moment Kanifnath saw King Gopichand, that very moment the fire of his anger flared up. But using discretion, he controlled his anger. He said in his mind “If we curse and turn him to ashes right now, the task to be achieved through him will remain incomplete. Also, what the condition of the Guru is, is also not known. Therefore, first take information and then punish.” With such a thought, he became calm. In the meantime, King Gopichand came near, fell at his feet and began to request in a piteous voice “Maharaj! By the grace of destiny, the flow of your river of mercy has turned towards me today to make me, an orphan, protected.” Hearing this humble speech of the King, Kanifa felt joy, he held the King's hand and made him sit beside him. Later he said “King! A great improper act has happened by your hand. But because your fortune is strong, my mind has become calm. Otherwise, a great disaster would have befallen you. Now come into the village, I will tell everything there.” Then the King made him sit in a palanquin and took him to the palace. He seated him on a golden throne, performed worship with sixteen-fold offerings, gave clothes and ornaments and began to ask for initiation.
kanifanathText3: He said “You wish to take my initiation, but like adding salt to milk, a sin has been committed by you. Those from whom I took initiation, that Jalindarnath you have buried in horse dung. But your life is long and your merit is powerful, therefore I became calm. Otherwise, Jalindarnath would have turned you to ashes in a single moment.” Hearing this, the King began to tremble. Falling at Kanifa's feet, he said “Maharaj! Please forgive my offence and have mercy on this servant.” Then Kanifa took him and went to his camp. This news the maidservants told to Mainavati; it also became known to other women. Mainavati felt extreme grief, but she felt that punishment should not fall upon her son. King Gopichand got fully engaged in Kanifa's service; he began to serve like a slave. Whatever Kanifa asked for, he provided with promptness.
kanifanathText4: In the evening, Kanifa ordered the King to go to the palace. The King first went to Mainavati and told the whole account. He said “You mediate so that Kanifa may forgive my offence.” Mainavati agreed to that. Later she went to Kanifa's camp and sat after falling at his feet. She said “I have made Jalindarnath my Guru.” Kanifa said “I too have made that same one my Guru. Then how did you allow such a state of his to happen?” Then Mainavati told the whole story. Finally she said “Forgive Gopichand's offences and take him under your wing. Save him from the wrath of Jalindarnath. Pull the Guru out of the pit and increase his fame.” Hearing this, Kanifa gave her a promise “I will plead with Jalindarnath and keep Gopichand fearless.” Then Mainavati came home and removed her son's fear.
kanifanathText5: After Mainavati took a promise from Kanifa and removed the fear in Gopichand's mind, the next morning King Gopichand went to the Nath's camp and stood with folded hands after placing his head on the feet. Then Kanifa asked the King, at which place have you buried Jalindarnath, show me that spot. Then the King became ready to show that place and to go and see that place, the Nath sent one of his disciples along with him. After the King returned after showing the spot to that disciple, Kanifa told the King that, now tell me by what trick you bring Jalindarmaharaj out of the pit. Hearing this, Gopichand prayed that, Maharaj! I understand nothing in this matter; I am entirely surrendered to you. After the King said thus with extreme humility, Kanifa suggested to him that, King, for the protection of your life, prepare five statues like yourself of these metals: gold, silver, copper, brass and iron.
kanifanathText6: The King got five statues prepared by craftsmen. Later, after seeing an auspicious time, Kanifnath and the King went to that place. Placing the gold statue in the center, the King started digging. A voice came from inside to tell the name. Saying ‘It is King Gopichand’, Jalindarnath gave a curse and the statue was burnt. In this same manner, all five statues were turned to ashes. Finally, at Kanifa's suggestion, the King started digging again. Then Jalindarnath considered and decided to make the King immortal. When Kanifa told his identity, Jalindarnath gave a blessing to Gopichand – “Let him remain in the world becoming immortal.” Then Jalindarnath himself removed the soil with the Vajrastra and came out. The meeting of Guru and disciple took place. Gopichand placed his head on his feet. Jalindarnath embraced him and gave the blessing of immortality.
jalindarNathText19: After this, Jalindarnath told Gopichand to ask for whatever he wanted. But royal glory is perishable. Hearing this, detachment arose in Gopichand's mind. He decided to accept the path of Yoga. Jalindarnath initiated him with a mantra and made him a recluse. He accepted the Naga sect by wearing matted hair, a loincloth, and the sacred rings.
jalindarNathText20: As soon as the news of the King becoming a recluse spread, there was mourning everywhere. Jalindarnath told him to go for penance and first ordered him to ask for alms from his wives. Gopichand went to ask for alms. The women tried very hard to stop him, but he refused them. Finally, Mainavati gave him alms. Gopichand returned to the Guru. After giving instructions for a few days, Jalindarnath ordered him to go to Badrikashram and perform severe penance for twelve years. Gopichand left immediately. His departure submerged the entire city in sorrow. Gopichand's son Muktachand was seated on the royal throne. Jalindarnath performed his coronation and arranged the state administration properly. After that, with Kanifa and his disciples, Jalindarnath stayed there for some time, made all arrangements smooth, and left. King Gopichand, by the order of Guru Jalindarnath, took detachment and set out for Badrikashram to perform penance. While going by the way, he maintained his livelihood by asking for alms. Hearing the news of the King becoming a recluse, people felt deep regret. Wherever he went, people insisted on stopping him, but he kept moving forward.
jalindarNathText21: After a few days, he went to Paulapattan city in Kaulbengal, where his sister Champavati was living. In her in-laws' house, Gopichand's detachment was being slandered. Hearing this, Champavati became sad. Meanwhile, Gopichand came to the city and sat at one place. The maidservants recognized him and told this news in the palace. King Tilakchand ordered to keep him in the horse stable. Gopichand began to eat food there peacefully. But hearing the slander against him, Champavati became overwhelmed with grief and committed suicide. As soon as this news was known, Gopichand became sad and began to consider himself responsible for his sister's death.
jalindarNathText22: While the corpse was being taken for cremation, Gopichand said, “Do not burn the corpse; I will bring Guru Jalindarnath and make her alive.” But no one listened to him. Then he sat on the funeral pyre and took an oath on the glory of the Guru. Finally, the people agreed to preserve the corpse for four days, but they cut off its hand and gave it to Gopichand. However, later they burnt the corpse. Gopichand set out to bring the Guru. As soon as Jalindarnath came to know of this incident, he met him himself. After Gopichand told the whole account, Jalindarnath promised to make Champavati alive. Both of them came to Paulapattan. Jalindarnath took Champavati's hand and made her alive with the Sanjivani mantra. She got up and fell at their feet. Seeing this, everyone was amazed and bowed at the feet of the Naths.
jalindarNathText23: Later, when Jalindarnath began to leave, King Tilakchand asked for forgiveness. Jalindarnath stayed there for one night, gave initiation to Champavati, and made her immortal. Also, he ordered Tilakchand to take care of the responsibility of the kingdom of Gopichand's son Muktachand. The next day, Gopichand set out for Badrikashram for penance. Jalindarnath went to Helapattan and stayed for some time. Then after twelve years, he went to Badrikashram, met Gopichand, and after completing the ceremony of his penance, gave him all knowledge and boons.
gorakshanathText10: Gorakshanath was a Yogi man. Who would give him entry into the kingdom of women? Therefore, he made friendship with a courtesan named Kalinga and convinced her that he was an excellent musician and decided to enter the kingdom of women in her company. The Queen of this kingdom was famous by names such as Padmini, Tilottama, Mainakini. Machindranath was immersed in her company. To free this Machindra, Gorakshanath entered the kingdom of women by wearing a woman's attire. He accepted the work of playing the mrdanga during the dance. From his mrdanga playing, the sound “Chalo Machindar Gorakh Aaya” began to come.
ovi11: मृदंग अक्षरीं तैसीं चर्या ॥ दावीतसे गुरुवर्या ॥ ” चलो मच्छिंदर गोरख आया ” ॥ पुन्हा अक्षरें आच्छादी ॥३४॥
machindranathText13: Hearing that, Machindranath was startled and he fell into thought as to how Gorakh came. By that sound, his facial expression fell and his mind was withdrawn from the song. Then Padmini asked the reason for this happening. Upon that, he informed her of the whole matter of Gorakshanath from the root. Later, Gorakh revealed his true form to Mainakini. Mainakini, considering him her eldest son, welcomed him well; but in this sensual pleasure, Gorakshanath found no peace. When he found an opportunity, he said to Machindranath in clear words,
ovi12: हे महाराज योगपती । आपण असतां या देशप्रती । परी हें अश्लाघ्य नाथपंधी । मातें योग्य दिसेना ॥ श्रीमूर्त्ति चांगुलपणें । महास्मशानीं करी स्थापन । तैसा येथें तुमच्चा वास जाण । दिसत आहे महाराजा ॥ पहा जी योगधर्मी । तुम्ही बैसलां निस्पृह होवोनी । तेणेंकरून ब्रह्मांड धामीं । कीर्तिध्वज उभारिला ॥ मृत्यु पाताळ एकवीस स्वर्ग । व्यापितें आहे जितुकें जग । तितुकें वांच्छिती आपुला योग । चरणरज सेवावया ॥ ऐसी प्रज्ञा प्रौढपणीं । असोनी पडावें गर्ते अवनीं । चिंताहारक चिंतामणी । अजाग्रींवीं शोभना ॥ तरी पाहे कृपाळु महाराज । उभारिला जो कीर्तिध्वज । कीं तोच मिरवेल तेजःपुंज । ऐसें करीं महाराजा ॥ कीं पूर्वी पाहा ब्रह्मस्थिती । श्रीकविनारायणाची होती । लोकोपकारा अवतार क्षितीं । जगामाजीं मिरवला ॥ ऐसें असता प्रौढपण । ते आचरावें धर्म । मग जगास बोल काय म्हणवावे । अर्धा अर्धी ठेवावे ? ॥ तेची तुम्ही दुष्कृत आचरता । लोकही आचरती तुम्हांदेखतां । अवतारदीक्षेलागीं माघां । दोष होईल जाणिजे ॥ तरी महाराजा ऐके वचन । सकल वैभव त्यजून । निःसंग व्हावें संगें करून । दुःखसरिता तरावी ॥ (२१.१८...३४)
machindranathText14: Seeing that his disciple was advising him, Machindranath's mind changed. Detachment arose in him. On the day of Chaitra Shuddha Pratipada, along with Minanath, Machindranath and Goraksha came out of the kingdom of women. Machindranath, Gorakshanath, and Minanath came to Jagannath and Saurashtra while on pilgrimage. One day, when Gorakshanath had gone for alms, Minanath was sleeping. After he woke up, Machindranath told Gorakshanath to wash him and bring him. Seeing Minanath dirty because he was young, an outburst of detachment arose in Gorakshanath's mind. Considering Machindranath's attachment to the kingdom of women, in anger he took Minanath to the river and killed him by dashing him against a rock. He threw his body into the water and only washed the skin and put it out to dry. When Machindranath returned, he asked where Minanath was. Gorakshanath showed the skin. Seeing that, Machindranath became extremely sad and began to lament. Then Gorakshanath said, “Guru-raja, why do you act in ignorance? That which is perishable has been destroyed, the eternal never dies.” But even then, Machindranath's grief did not stop. Finally, as soon as Gorakshanath threw sacred ash with the Sanjivani mantra, Minanath became alive. He got up and began to embrace Machindranath. Then everyone felt joy. Further, Gorakshanath said, “Even though you are so powerful, what is the reason for crying?” Upon that, Machindranath said, “Tell me why you killed him.” Gorakshanath said, “To see your affection.” Then Machindranath said, “To test the hope-desire and knowledge-ignorance within you, I also performed this experiment.” Hearing this, Gorakshanath became humble and said that, “All this happened only by your grace,” and he placed his head at the Guru's feet.
machindranathText15: Further, Machindranath and Gorakshanath, along with Minanath, left Saurashtra and came to Tailangana. There, they bathed at the Godavari confluence, performed Shiva worship, and further visiting various holy places reached the place of Valmiki Rishi on Garbhagiri mountain. That forest was extremely terrifying. In Machindranath's bag was a gold brick given by Queen Mainakini. Fearing that it would be stolen, he repeatedly began to ask Gorakshanath, “Is there no fear of thieves?” Gorakshanath considered it in his mind and made a remedy. At one place when the Guru went for toilet, he took out the gold brick from the bag and put a stone in its place. Further, when Machindranath asked about the fear, Gorakshanath said, “The fear that was there has remained behind.” Later, upon checking the bag, seeing that the brick was not there, Machindranath became very sad and began to speak to Gorakshanath in anger. Still, Gorakshanath remained calm. He went up the mountain and urinated with mantra power and that entire mountain became golden. Seeing that, Machindranath said, “When a philosopher's stone like you is near, what is the need for gold!” and he praised Gorakshanath. When Gorakshanath asked the Guru's intention, Machindranath said that, “After going to our country, we should worship saints and sages and perform a great feast, therefore I had kept the gold brick carefully.” Hearing this, Gorakshanath said, “I will fulfill this intention of yours.” He threw sacred ash towards the heaven with the Gandharvastra mantra. Along with that, Chitrasena Gandharva appeared. Gorakshanath ordered him to send Gandharvas in all directions and call the recluses, ascetics, chanters, meditators, saints, gods, Gandharvas, demons, and Kinnaras. Chitrasena sent a hundred Gandharvas. Navnath, Shukracharya, Dattatreya, Yajnavalkya, Vashistha, Vamadeva, Kapila, Vyasa, Parashara, Narada, Valmiki, and other groups of sages reached there in a short time.
ovi13: मग त्या गंधर्वासी चित्रसेने ॥ सांगूनि सर्व वर्तमान ॥ दाही दिशा प्रेरणा करुन ॥ प्रज्ञावंत आणिले कीं ॥४॥ जपी तपी योगशीळ ॥ गुप्त प्रगट आणिले सकळ ॥ नवनाथादि ऋषिमंडळ ॥ येऊनियां पोहोंचले ॥५॥ शुक दत्तात्रेय याज्ञवल्की ॥ वसिष्ठ वामदेव कपिल शेखी ॥ व्यास पाराशर नारद ऋषी ॥ वाल्मीक पाचारिले गंधर्वी ॥६॥ अठ्यायशीं सहस्त्र ऋषिभार ॥ स्वर्गीहूनि उतरले देवकिन्नर ॥ गणगंधर्वदि वसुलोक अपार ॥ तपोलोक पातले ॥७॥ त्यांतचि अष्टवसूंपहित ॥ उपरिचर आला विमानव्यक्त ॥ तेणें येतंाचि मच्छिंद्रास वृत्तांत ॥ कीलोतळेचा सांगीतला ॥८॥ ऐसे वदतां उभय जाण ॥ तों देवांसह उतरला पाकशासन ॥ ब्रह्मा विष्णु रुद्रादि पूर्ण ॥ महीलागीं उतरले ॥१२॥ श्रीनाथासी भेटोनि सकळ ॥ मग ठाई ठाई सर्व मंडळ ॥ विराजूनि वार्ता सकळ ॥ ठाई ठाई करिताती ॥१३॥
machindranathText16: After this, Gorakshanath told the Guru that a great meal ceremony is ready. He called the Ashtasiddhis and gave them the arrangement of cooking and prepared excellent delicacies. All arrangements were extremely grand and everyone felt joy. Gahininath was not in this ceremony. Then Gorakshanath asked the Guru. Machindranath sent a Gandharva to Madhu-brahmana and asked to bring Gahininath. The Gandharva went and gave the message to the brahmana. He joyfully took Gahininath and came to Garbhadri mountain. Seven-year-old Gahininath was placed at Machindranath's feet. Machindranath lovingly took him close and told everyone that he is an incarnation of Karabhanjana Narayana. At that time, Shankara told Machindranath that, “I will later take an incarnation by the name of Nivritti and this Gahininath will give him initiation; therefore, make him capable by teaching all sciences.” Hearing this, Machindranath got initiation given to Gahininath through Gorakshanath and placed his hand of blessing on his head in the presence of the gods. This ceremony lasted for one month. Later, Gorakshanath asked Kubera to bring clothes and ornaments in exchange for the golden mountain. Kubera brought many clothes and ornaments. They were distributed to all and after satisfying everyone, they were seen off with honor. After this, Minanath was sent with Uparichara Vasu to Singhaladvipa to his mother Tilottama. She accepted the son with love; however, as the hope of meeting Machindranath remained unfulfilled, tears came to her eyes. Giving her courage, Uparichara Vasu left and she joyfully began to nurture the child.
machindranathText17: Gorakshanath and Machindranath remained on Garbhadri mountain for Gahininath's education. Umakanta was also there. Kubera hid the golden mountain with Adrushyastra; but Shankara remained right there, who is called ‘Mhatardev’ (Vriddheshwar). In that area, various Naths made their residence—Kanifnath in the west (Madhi), Machindranath in the south, Jalindarnath in the east, and further Naganath and Revansiddha lived at Vite. Gorakshanath lived at Vamatirtha and began to give education to Gahininath. In one year, Gahininath became proficient in all sciences and was sent back to Madhu-brahmana. Later, the Naths took Samadhi right there.
ovi14: परी गर्भाद्रि पर्वतांत ॥ वस्तीस राहिला उमाकांत ॥ तो अद्यापि आहे स्वस्थानांत ॥ म्हातारदेव म्हणती त्या ॥६५॥ तयाचिया पश्चिम दिशेसी ॥ कानिफा राहिला शिष्यकटकेंसी ॥ वस्ती करोनि नाम या ग्रामासी ॥ मढी
