ऐसें ठेविलें ॥६६॥ तयाचे दक्षिण पर्वतीं ॥ राहता झाला मच्छिंद्र जती ॥ त्याहूनि पूर्वेस महीपर्वतीं ॥ जालिंदर राहिला ॥६७॥ आणि त्या पर्वतापैलदेशीं ॥ नागनाथ राहिला वडावानळेंशीं ॥ आणि रेवणासिद्ध जया महाशीं ॥ विटेग्रामीं राहिला ॥६८॥ वामतीर्थ गर्भाद्रिपर्वतीं ॥ राहता झाला गोरक्ष जती ॥ सेवेसी शिष्य ठेवोनि सप्ती ॥ विद्या सागे गाहिनीते ॥६९॥ एक वर्षपर्यंत ॥ अभ्यासिला गाहिनीनाथ ॥ सकळ विद्येचे स्वसामर्थ्य ॥ तया देहीं सांठविलें ॥१७०॥ परी कोंतीगांवी मधुब्राह्मण ॥ गेले होते गहिनीस ठेवोन ॥ ते जालंदरासमीप दिशेकारण ॥ वस्तीलागीं विराजले ॥७१॥ विराजले परी गहिनीनाथ ॥ अभ्यासिते झाले पात्रभरित ॥ मग गोरक्ष बोळवोनि त्यातें ॥ विप्रापाशीं पाठविला ॥७२॥ यावरी त्या वस्तीस ॥ वसते झाले बहुत दिवस ॥ शके दहाशें वर्षांस ॥ समाधीं त्यांनी घेतल्या ॥७३॥ घेतल्या परी यवनधर्म ॥ कबरव्यक्त झाले आश्रम ॥ पुढें औरंगजेब तें पाहून ॥ पुसता झाला लोकांसी ॥७४॥ ह्या कोणाच्या असती कबरी ॥ ते म्हणती तव पूर्वजांच्या साचारीं ॥ मठींत कान्हाबापर्वती मच्छिंद्र ॥ आवडतें स्थान याचें तें ॥७५॥ त्याहूनि पूर्वेस जालिंदर ॥ विराजली त्याची कबर ॥ त्याहूनि खालता बल्ली थोर ॥ गाहिनीनाथ नांदतसे ॥७६॥ मग तेणें ऐकूनि ऐसी भात ॥ पालटिलें त्या नांवातें ॥ जानपीर जालिंदरातें ॥ ठेविलें असे राजानें ॥७७॥ गाहिनीनाथास गैवी पीर ॥ नाम ठेविलें तेवी साचार ॥ महीजदी बांधोनि पुजारे ॥ ठाई ठाई स्थापिले ॥७८॥ मच्छिंद्र आणि कानिफाचें ॥ नामाभिधान बदलूनि साचें ॥ मायावा कान्होबा बोलोनि साचें ॥ यवन पुजारी स्थापिले ॥७९॥ कल्याण कलबुगीं बाबाचैतन्य ॥ राजबागशर नाम ठेविलें त्यानें ॥ म्हणाल केलें यवनकारण ॥ ऐसें विपरीत त्या रायें ॥१८०॥ परी समाधी पाहिल्या कबरीऐशा ॥ म्हणोनि त्यातें पडला भास ॥ कीं हे पीर असतील यवनकुळींचे ॥ म्हणोनि प्रविष्ट करावें ॥८१॥ म्हणोनि ऐसें कृत्य घडलें ॥ यापरी ऐकोनि श्रोता बोले ॥ कीं कबरयुक्त नाथ केले भले ॥ काय म्हणोनि झालेती ॥८२॥ तरी ते अंतरसाक्ष नाथ ॥ यवन राजे होतील महीते ॥ ते छळितील हिंदूदेवांतें ॥ म्हणोनि कबरी बांधिल्या ॥८३॥ परी हें असो आतां कथन ॥ मध्यें कथा असती देदीप्यमान ॥ नाथांनीं योजूनि आपुलालें स्थान ॥ ठाई ठाई राहिले ॥८४॥ गोरक्ष सटव्या ठेवोनि रक्षण ॥ निघता झाला तीर्थांकारण ॥ त्या सटव्या तेथें अद्याप राहून ॥ रक्षिताती स्थानासी ॥८५॥
bhartariNathText1: One day in the evening, as Surya (the Sun) and Urvashi's eyes met, Surya was overcome by lust, leading to the discharge of semen. As that semen fell from the sky, it was split into two parts by the wind. One part fell into a pot (ghata) in the ashram of Lomesh Rishi, from which the body of Agastya was born. The second part came to the ashram of Kaulik Rishi. At that time, he was going out to ask for alms. He was placing his alms-bowl in the courtyard and closing the door. In that interval, that semen came and fell into it. This came to the Rishi's sight. At that time, he understood that this semen belonged to Surya. After three thousand one hundred and three years pass, Dhrumin-Narayana will enter into this vessel; therefore, this must be kept carefully, thinking thus, he kept that alms-bowl safely. After many years passed since this event, later the Kaliyuga began. Then that Rishi kept that vessel in a cave of Mandarachal. Later, after three thousand one hundred and three years of Kali passed, the Lord of Dwarka entered that vessel in the incarnation of Dhrumin-Narayana. That fetus kept growing and as soon as nine months were complete, a statue was ready and the vessel broke, and from it, a child as brilliant as the sun came out. At the same time, some deer came there. One doe was pregnant; she had two fawns, but she saw three, so she began to nurture all three. Initially, that child did not know how to drink; still, she raised him with ingenuity. Later he began to crawl and lived with the doe for five years.
bhartariNathText2: One day as those four came onto the path, Jaysingh Bhat and his wife Renuka saw that brilliant child. Jaysingh decided to catch him and take him home. The child was crying for the doe and the doe was also coming behind; but she was not coming near due to fear. Jaysingh took the child away and later he began to learn speaking and walking. That Bhat took him to Kashi. There, at the time of the darshan of Vishweshwara, words came out of the Lingam—'Come, Bhartari!' Based on this, that child's name was kept as Bhartari. Jaysingh and Renuka loved him very much and began to raise him excellently. Because Bhartari had the Rajayoga (destiny for kingship), he used to play games by becoming a king among children. One day while playing, he fell down and became unconscious. The children fled in fear. Then Surya himself came, picked him up, fed him, and restored his body to its previous state, and bringing him home in the guise of a Brahmin, handed him over. Upon Renuka's inquiry, Surya revealed his identity, told the complete story of Bhartari, and asked to continue his upbringing. Then he left. Jaysingh also felt joy upon understanding this incident and loved Bhartari completely. When Bhartari became sixteen years old, they left from Kashi; but on the way, thieves killed Jaysingh and looted the wealth. After that, Renuka also died of grief. Bhartari performed the cremation of both and became destitute, submerged in sorrow. Then some merchants gave him support and taking him with them, consoled him. In their company, he slowly began to forget his grief. Further, they reached Avanti-nagari with him.
bhartariNathText3: After Bhartarinath arrived at Avanti-nagar in the company of the merchants, they stayed near a village. There, having arranged the goods properly, all sat in one place lighting a fire. Just then, jackals came and gave a signal that thieves were about to attack. Because Bhartari understood the language of animals, he alerted the merchants. They kept watch fully armed and defeated the thieves. Further, the jackals again said that a strong demon was coming, and the one who kills him and applies a mark (tilak) of his blood will become the King of Avanti. Vikram hears this and he slays the demon. That demon was previously Chitrama Gandharva, who had become a demon due to the curse of Parvati. Due to the boon of Shankara, his liberation happened at the hands of Vikram. After killing the demon, Vikram found four jewels in its fist. Vikram realizes the greatness of Bhartari and considers bringing him near himself. With the help of a tax collector, he brings Bhartari to his home. Further, Bhartari begins to live with Vikram, and Vikram and his mother love him like a son.
bhartariNathText4: In Avanti-nagar, a king named Shubhavikram was ruling. He had only one daughter named Sumedhavati. She was extremely beautiful. One day while she was sitting on her father's lap, the thought of getting her married came to his mind. Later he brought up the matter with the minister that Sumedhavati had come of age, therefore a suitable groom for her beauty should be searched and seen. Upon that speech, Sumantik the minister said that they have reached old age and have no son; therefore, after finding a suitable groom for the daughter, she should be given by seating him on the throne. The son-in-law will be just like a son and the state will run properly.
bhartariNathText5: The King agreed to this plan. He said that a garland should be given in the elephant's trunk, and the one on whose neck he places it shall be given the kingdom and the daughter. After erecting a large pavilion, the elephant was released. The elephant roamed throughout the city, came near the fort, and among the guards there, placed the garland on Vikram's neck. He was brought with great pomp; but there was talk among the people that he is a potter. Upon the minister's inquiry, Kamat the potter said that Vikram's mother is Satyavati (the daughter of King Satyavarma of Mithila-nagari) and his father is Surochan Gandharva. Hearing this, the King was pleased. After bringing King Satyavarma, all doubts were cleared. Vikram's coronation was performed and his marriage with Sumedhavati took place. Further, King Satyavarma also gave his kingdom to him.
bhartariNathText6: Vikram became the King and Bhartari became the crown prince. The minister decided to give his daughter Pingala to Bhartari. Upon searching for his caste, Bhartari told that he is the son of Surya. Then he prayed to Surya, and Surya came to Avanti-nagar and cleared everyone's doubts. The marriage took place with great pomp. The gods showered flowers and Surochan Gandharva also came. Bhartari later married many women; Pingala was the chief queen. He became immersed in sensual pleasures. Seeing this, Surya requested Dattatreya. Dattatreya said that he will bless Bhartari by making him a Nathpanthi. One day Bhartrihari went hunting. Due to the intense sun, water was not found. The entire army became overwhelmed with thirst. Then Dattatreya created an illusory lake. As Bhartrihari went to drink water, Dattatreya stopped him and asked—who are you, who is your Guru?
bhartariNathText7: Bhartrihari told his story. Since he had no Guru, Dattatreya called him impure and ordered him not to drink water. Bhartrihari prayed. Then Dattatreya said to perform penance for twelve years. The King said that he was not yet free from the world. Finally, Dattatreya gave him water to drink, gave him a mantra, and revealed his own identity. Then the lake became invisible. Dattatreya created water from Bhogavati and food from Kamadhenu and satisfied everyone. Bhartrihari returned to his city with the army and Dattatreya disappeared. After giving the initiation in the forest, Bhartrihari asked Dattatreya for a period of twelve years to lead a worldly life. After getting it, he went to Ujjaini and after having dinner at night, went to Pingala's palace. As soon as he entered the palace, Pingala seated him on a floral bed on a golden couch, worshipped him, and expressed her love for the King. They both sat very close and began to have humorous conversations. Then the King seated her on his left thigh, kissed her, and spoke many words about his love. Later Pingala gave him a betel leaf (tambool) and said that our love has become entirely one; but there is a fear of death. Only if I die before you will I be considered fortunate. On this, Bhartrihari said that all this is under God's control; but if I die first, what will you do? Then Pingala said that I will not remain alive after you; I will offer my body into the fire. The King expressed doubt on her words, but Pingala stated firmly that she would not remain a widow. Hearing this, the King decided to test her.
bhartariNathText8: One day after going hunting, he killed a deer, applied its blood on his clothes, and giving them to a servant, told him to tell Pingala that a tiger has killed the King. The servant went to Avanti and gave the message to Pingala. Hearing this, Pingala's condition became extremely miserable. She began to cry. As soon as this news spread in the palace, all the women began to lament. Finally, Pingala decided to go Sati. She went to the cremation ground and jumped into the fire-pit to become Sati. Here, while the King was returning, bad doubts began to come to him. Upon coming into the city, as soon as he learned the news that Pingala had gone Sati, he became overwhelmed with grief. He went to the cremation ground and was prepared to jump into the fire himself; but people stopped him. He kept crying in the grief of Pingala. People consoled him; but he did not listen to anything. Finally, everyone left and Bhartrihari remained sitting in the cremation ground. He began to spend his days without food and water. When King Vikram got this news, he came to Ujjaini. He tried to console Bhartrihari; but it was of no use. After ten days, after performing the funeral rites for Pingala, Vikram started the administration of the state. Even though twelve years passed, Bhartrihari did not come out of the grief. He gave up food and began to live by taking only leaves and water. His body became lean.
bhartariNathText9: Seeing this condition, Surya felt pity. He went to Dattatreya and requested him to have mercy on Bhartrihari. Then Dattatreya consoled him and said that he would bring Bhartrihari to the right path by sending Gorakshanath, the disciple of Machindranath.
gorakshanathText11: After the ceremony on Garbhagiri mountain was over, Gorakshanath, while on pilgrimage and according to the command of Shri Prabhu Dattatreya, took Bhartrihari and went to Girinar mountain to meet Dattatreya. They stayed there for three days. Then, taking the permission of Dattatreya, Gorakshanath set out to go to Machindranath. At that time, Dattatreya told Gorakshanath, “Many days have passed, and I have not met Machindranath; therefore, bring him once to meet me.”
machindranathText18: Taking Dattatreya's message, Gorakshanath came to Garbhagiri, met Machindranath, and told him the entire account. Then, after a few days, both set out for the darshan of Dattatreya. While traveling, they reached Kaundinyapur in the Vaidarbha country. While asking for alms there, they saw a strange incident: King Shashangar had cut off his son's limbs and thrown him at a crossroads. Despite the King being wise, generous, and powerful, why had he become so cruel? Due to the anger of the stepmother, Prince Krishnagar's limbs had been cut off. He was lying on a chaurang (wooden stool) in a limb-less state. Seeing this, Machindranath and Gorakshanath felt pity. They took Chauranginath with them and went to seat him for penance in Badrikavan. After seating Chauranginath for penance, Machindranath and Gorakshanath left that place and went to Girinar mountain for the darshan of Dattatreya. Upon seeing Machindranath, Dattatreya felt supreme joy. It was a loving meeting, as if a child were meeting its mother. Both lovingly talked about joys and sorrows. Dattatreya held them close and said, “Stay here now, do not go on pilgrimage.” Both stayed there for six months. Later, they asked for permission to go on pilgrimage. Then Machindranath said, “We have taken birth for the salvation of the world; therefore, it is not possible for us to stay in one place.” Hearing this, Dattatreya gave them permission to leave. While taking leave, tears of love began to flow from the eyes of all three.
machindranathText19: Leaving from there and going in the direction of Kashi, they came to Prayag. At that time, a king named Trivikram was ruling there. He was extremely wise, courageous, and generous; but he was depressed in mind because he had no offspring. His queen, Revati, was a devoted wife, but she too was dejected because they had no children. In time, the King passed away. There was a great outcry throughout the kingdom. People began to cry, and the Queen was submerged in a sea of sorrow. At such a time, Machindranath and Gorakshanath came to that city. Seeing this state, compassion arose in Machindranath's heart. He thought, “One should bring such a dear King back to life and remove everyone's sorrow.” But from a Yogic perspective, that King had merged into the Brahman-form, so it was impossible to give him life again. Therefore, Machindranath began to return from there. However, Gorakshanath's mind was distressed by the people's sorrow. He wanted to free the people from that suffering; still, by the Guru's command, he moved forward with Machindranath. In that quiet Shiva temple outside the village, where Gorakshanath and Machindranath had sat for shelter, the atmosphere had become very grave. Nearby, in the cremation ground, a large crowd had gathered for the final rites of King Trivikram's dead body. Outcry, lamentation, and the shadow of sorrow were spread everywhere. Seeing this scene, Gorakshanath's heart felt pain. He could not bear the people's sorrow. He requested Guru Machindranath, “Bring this King back to life and end everyone's sorrow.” But Machindranath gestured to him to remain quiet. Still, the compassion in Gorakshanath's heart did not stop. He said firmly, “If you do not do it, I myself will bring this King to life. And if I cannot do that, I will jump into the fire and give up my life.” Hearing this, Machindranath became grave. He explained that the King had merged into the Brahman-form, so bringing him back to life was not easily possible. But when Gorakshanath looked with insight, he accepted this truth, yet the vow he had taken would not let him back down. Then Machindranath suggested a miraculous remedy—“I myself will enter this King's dead body. But you protect my original body for twelve years.” Gorakshanath accepted this remedy. Then Machindranath, through Yogic power, left his body and entered King Trivikram's dead body. At that very moment, the King sat up in the cremation ground. People were astonished and filled with joy. They celebrated the occasion. Meanwhile, Gorakshanath searched for a secret place to keep his Guru's original body safe. He got the help of a Gurvini (temple servant). Under her guidance, he hid the body in a cellar in the Shiva temple and asked her to keep the whole matter secret. During that time, Machindranath began to rule in the form of King Trivikram. Everything was going smoothly. After a few days, Gorakshanath went away on a pilgrimage. Time passed. Queen Revati became pregnant and gave birth to a son—Dharmanath. One day while she was worshipping in the Shiva temple, she prayed, “May I die while my husband is still alive.” Hearing this prayer, the Gurvini laughed. When the Queen asked the reason, she revealed the whole secret—that the current King is not the real Trivikram but Machindranath, and his original body is kept in the cellar. Hearing this, fear arose in Revati's mind. She thought that after twelve years, Machindranath would return to his original body, and then her and her son's future would be in danger. Therefore, she took a harsh decision. One midnight, she took a maidservant, went to the cellar, cut Machindranath's original body into pieces, and threw them out.
machindranathText20: As soon as this happened, Goddess Parvati became aware and informed Lord Shankara. Shankara immediately ordered the Yakshinis and Chamundas to collect the pieces of the body and keep them safe. They took the pieces to Kailash and handed them over to Virabhadra. Virabhadra appointed countless Shivaganas, Yakshinis, and Chamundas to guard the body very strictly, for they knew that Gorakshanath, the great Yogi, would surely come to get his Guru's body back. Here, Machindranath, in the form of Trivikram, would go to the cellar every day to check, but since everything looked as before, he had no idea of this event. While Gorakshanath had gone on pilgrimage, he was completely unaware of the serious event that had happened behind him—that Revati had cut Machindranath's body into pieces, and Parvati had had those pieces collected by Yakshinis and kept safe on Kailash in Virabhadra's custody.
machindranathText21: Meanwhile, while wandering, Gorakshanath reached a desolate forest near Bhamanagar on the banks of the Godavari. He was experiencing intense hunger and thirst. Not a drop of water was to be found. While wandering in such a state, he saw an innocent ten-year-old boy working in the field; his name was Manik. Just as the boy was about to sit down for a meal, Gorakshanath arrived and said, “Aadesh.” Hearing that divine word, Manik immediately stood up, bowed at his feet, and asked with great respect, “Maharaj, who are you? How did you come to this desolate place?” Gorakshanath said, “I am a Jati (ascetic). I am very hungry and thirsty. Can some arrangement for food and water be made?” Hearing this, Manik served them food with great love, gave water, and provided excellent hospitality. Gorakshanath was satisfied. After the meal, Gorakshanath was pleased and asked, “Child, what is your name?” Manik answered humbly, “Maharaj, your work is done, right? Then what is the meaning in asking the name now? It was appropriate to ask before the work, but now it is useless.” Hearing this, Gorakshanath became introspective. He said, “I am pleased with your service. If you have any wish, ask, and I will fulfill it.” Manik said with a smile, “Maharaj, you yourself live by asking for alms, so what will you give me? Instead, if you need something, tell me, and I will give it.” Gorakshanath thought—this boy is innocent, but he should be tested. He said, “Fine. Then I ask only one thing from you—renounce all those things that you feel like doing.” Hearing this, Manik accepted that vow joyfully. Gorakshanath left from there. But the effect of that vow was extraordinary. When Manik set out to go home, he remembered Gorakshanath's vow—“Do not do that which you desire.” He felt a desire to go home, so he stopped. Then he felt like moving his body, but he did not move a limb. He felt like eating, but he did not eat. In this way, he controlled all his desires. Time passed. He stood in one place like that—no food, no water. Only consuming air and chanting the name of Ram. Gradually his body became lean. The blood dried up, the flesh disappeared. Skin and bones became one. Yet he remained motionless—as if like a piece of lifeless wood, but the remembrance of the Supreme Soul was going on continuously in his heart.
machindranathText22: Here, Gorakshanath reached Badrikashram. There he saw the condition of Chauranginath—he was sitting in a cave performing penance. An anthill had formed around him, but the “Ram-nam” was going on continuously from his mouth. Gorakshanath brought him out, cast a merciful glance, and he regained his strength. After this, Gorakshanath took him and came to Kaundanyapur in the Vaidarbha country. There, Chauranginath showed his glory to his parents. With the Vatastra (wind weapon), he destroyed the entire garden and blew the army into the sky. Finally, he revealed his identity to his father. King Shashangar was overjoyed to see his son.
machindranathText23: After this, both came to Prayag. There, Gorakshanath asked the Gurvini about Machindranath's body. Upon learning from her mouth about the act committed by Queen Revati, immense anger erupted in Gorakshanath's heart. But he maintained restraint and determined to search for the Guru's body. Gorakshanath took a subtle form and searched the entire Earth, the netherworld, and Heaven. Finally, he reached Kailash. There he saw the pieces of Machindranath's body; at that time, Virabhadra was telling the Shivaganas—“The twelve-year period is complete; now protect Machindranath's body with extreme caution. Because there is no telling when or in what form his disciple Gorakshanath will come to search.” As soon as these words of Virabhadra reached Gorakshanath's ears, he left from there and entered his body again. Then Gorakshanath and Chauranginath deliberated, took sacred ash and the bag (jholi) in hand, and prepared for war. Gorakshanath first used the Parvatastra (mountain weapon) on Surya, which stopped Surya's chariot. Then Surya broke that Parvatastra with the Vajrastra and came to Gorakshanath himself to find out who was creating such an obstacle. So that the intense heat of the Sun would not be bearable, Gorakshanath used the Chandrastra (moon weapon) and created ten million moons, which produced coolness. After this, both Gorakshanath and Chauranginath fell at Surya's feet. Surya asked—“What is the reason for stopping me?” Upon that, Gorakshanath said, “The Shivaganas have taken Machindranath's body to Kailash. Our request is that you mediate and get it back for us.” At Gorakshanath's request, Surya agreed to mediate and went to Kailash. There the Shivaganas welcomed him and asked the reason for his arrival. Surya, on behalf of Gorakshanath, requested the return of Machindranath's body and described Gorakshanath's power. But it had no effect on Virabhadra. He said, “Machindranath caused us great distress and put our lives in danger. Such an enemy has easily come into our hands, so we will not release him even if our lives go. If Gorakshanath comes for war, we will make his condition the same.” Hearing this, Surya said, “If you had so much power, where was it when Machindranath defeated you previously? Now that he is in your hands, you are being arrogant. But Machindranath and Gorakshanath are both equally powerful. Moreover, Gorakshanath now has the support of Chauranginath. Therefore, this persistence is not right.” Still, Virabhadra flatly refused to return the body. Then Surya said, “The war should happen on Earth instead of on Kailash, otherwise Kailash will be destroyed,” and after saying this, he left.
machindranathText24: After Surya left, Virabhadra ordered the Shivaganas to go forward for war. Accordingly, the Ashtabhairavas, Ganas, and countless other troops came for war. Seeing seventy-two crore eighty-four lakh Ganas ready with weapons, Gorakshanath and Chauranginath also got ready. A fierce war started from both sides. Finally, due to Chauranginath's Mohini and Vatastra, Virabhadra's army suffered a major defeat. Then Virabhadra descended onto the battlefield with the Chamundas. Seeing the defeat of his army, he became enraged and pounced upon Gorakshanath. A terrible war began between the two. There was a massive barrage of weapons. But Virabhadra's weapons proved ineffective before Gorakshanath's power. Finally, Gorakshanath used the Sanjivani mantra and awakened many powerful demons—Tripura, Mahishasura, Jalandhar, Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Hiranyakashipu, etc., appeared on the battlefield. Seeing this scene, the thirty-three crore gods fled in fear and went to Vaikuntha to tell the whole account to Vishnu. Vishnu called Shankara and explained the situation. Both went together to Gorakshanath and began to reason with him. But Gorakshanath said firmly, “Return my Guru's body to me, only then will the dispute end.” Finally, Shankara sent the Chamundas to fetch Machindranath's body and handed it over to Gorakshanath and asked him to make the demons disappear. Then Gorakshanath said, “These demons have been awakened by the Sanjivani mantra. It is necessary to destroy them.” Shankara and Vishnu agreed. At that time, Virabhadra was still fighting the demons. Seeing that, Gorakshanath used the Vatakarsana Astra. As he threw the sacred ash while chanting the mantra, all the demons along with Virabhadra fell unconscious on the ground. Shankara and Vishnu praised Gorakshanath. Then Gorakshanath incinerated them all with the Agnyastra (fire weapon). This Vatakarsana experiment was so miraculous that it was not known even to gods and demons, except for the Nathpanth. After Virabhadra was burnt to ashes in the war, Shankara became extremely grief-stricken. The burning pain of the loss of a son was surging in his heart. Seeing this scene, Gorakshanath's heart melted. He thought to himself—“At the time when I was sitting for penance in Badrikashram, Shankara took care of me like a mother and bestowed immense grace upon me. It is not right for me to see such a master submerged in sorrow because of me today.” Bringing this thought to mind, Gorakshanath fell at Shankara's feet and said, “You are very sad at Virabhadra's death. But if I get his bones, I will bring him to life again. I would have raised him earlier with the Sanjivani mantra; but because he was burnt among the group of demons, all the demons would also rise again if I did so.” Hearing this, Shankara went to the battlefield. He searched for those bones that were chanting the ‘Shiva-nam’—identifying them as Virabhadra's, he brought them to Gorakshanath. Gorakshanath prepared the Sanjivani mantra, threw sacred ash, and in an instant, Virabhadra became alive. As soon as he rose, he began to say, “Where are my bow and arrows? Now I will destroy all the demons and finally send Gorakshanath to Yamapuri as well!” Then Shankara stopped him, told him the whole incident, and established a friendship between him and Gorakshanath. Just then, seventy-two crore eighty-four lakh Shivaganas, who roam with the speed of wind, saluted Gorakshanath and returned to Kailash. Gorakshanath came to the Shiva temple taking Machindranath's body.
machindranathText25: Here, King Trivikram (Machindranath) was immersed in royal pleasures. One day, he went to the Shiva temple as usual, where he saw Gorakshanath sitting with the pieces of his body. He inquired lovingly. When Gorakshanath told the whole account, he became very distressed. He said, “Have patience for a few days. I will come after seating Dharmanath on the throne.” Saying this, he went to the palace. Finding an auspicious moment, he performed Dharmanath's coronation and gave abundant charity to the seekers. After one month, one day, leaving King Trivikram's body, Machindranath entered his original body. In the palace, however, seeing the King lying dead, the Queen wailed. A pall of gloom spread throughout the city. As soon as Gorakshanath heard this news, he gathered the bones and flesh through the Sanjivani process, and in the meantime, Machindranath entered the body and sat up. Here, Queen Revati told the truth to Dharmanath—“Your father is Machindranath.” Hearing this, Dharmanath went to the Shiva temple, fell at their feet, and brought them to the palace. Staying there for one year, Machindranath, Gorakshanath, and Chauranginath set out on a pilgrimage. Dharmanath was ready to come with them, but Machindranath reasoned with him—“I will return after twelve years, then I will initiate you.” The three moved forward.
machindranathText26: During the pilgrimage, they came to Dhamanagar on the banks of the Godavari. There, Gorakshanath remembered the farmer Manik. The three went to him. He was standing like a piece of wood—there was no flesh on his body, but the Ram-nam was going on in his mouth. Seeing his penance, Gorakshanath made a plan. Recognizing his habit of giving opposing answers, he requested him to become a Guru. As expected, Manik gave the opposite answer—“You become my Guru.” At that very moment, Gorakshanath initiated him with a mantra. He attained enlightenment and fell at their feet. Giving him the name ‘Andabhang’, he was given the Nath initiation. Gorakshanath made him proficient in all sciences. After this, they came to Prayag. There, a son was born to Dharmanath—his name was kept Trivikram. Dharmanath decided to seat his son on the throne and take Yoga initiation himself. On the ‘Dharmanath Beej’ day, the death anniversary in the month of Magha, Gorakshanath initiated Dharmanath. On that day, gods, saints, and subjects gathered in large numbers. Everyone took the prasad and expressed joy. Everyone desired that this festival should be celebrated every year. Gorakshanath also gave the command accordingly. From that day on, the ‘Dharmanath Beej’ festival began to be celebrated every year.
machindranathText27: Gorakshanath has written in his ‘Kimayagiri’ text—whoever performs this Beej vow according to their strength, poverty, disease, and obstacles will not even touch their life. Their worldly life will be happy and Lakshmi will reside in their home. Such is the glory of ‘Dharmanath Beej’.
revannathText1: From the divine resolve of Lord Brahmadev, eighty-eight thousand Rishis were created in the past. At the very moment of that creation, a portion of their semen fell on the earth on the banks of the Reva river. In that divine sand, Chamsanarayana entered, and from that union, a miraculous statue was formed. As soon as that statue became alive, it lit up with a brilliant light like the sun. Right from birth, he began to cry, as if it were a proclamation of his existence. At the same time, a Kunbi (farmer) named Sahan Sarukh had come to the riverside to fetch water. In his sight, he saw that brilliant child lying in the sand. His heart was filled with compassion by that sight. He immediately picked up that child and brought him home. Before his wife, he said that they have received a son in the desert of the Reva river. His wife also joyfully accepted the child, bathed him, and laid him in the cradle next to her own son. Because he was found on the banks (tira) of the Reva, the child was named “Revannath”. Time passed. Revannath grew up gradually. As soon as he gained understanding, he began to go to the fields with his adopted father to work. Being only twelve years old, he became proficient in agricultural work.
revannathText2: One day at dawn, in an environment bathed in moonlight, Revannath was taking the oxen to graze in the forest. There was a glitter of stars in the sky and the path was clearly visible. In that quiet moment, suddenly Dattatreya appeared before him. Wooden sandals on his feet, a loincloth on his body, overgrown matted hair, a brownish beard and mustache — such was his brilliant, Trimurti-like incarnation. He was going towards Girinar mountain. As soon as Revannath saw him, a miraculous awakening occurred in his heart. He remembered his previous birth. Who we were, who we are now, and why we have fallen into ignorance — with these thoughts, his mind became distressed. He stood motionless. Then Dattatreya asked him, “Who are you?” Then Revannath said humbly, “In your body reside the portions of the Trinity. Out of those three qualities (Trigunas), I am the portion that is Sattvic. But currently, I am suffering in this body, trapped by ignorance. Please free me from this state.” Saying this, he placed his head at Dattatreya's feet. Seeing his faith and determination, Dattatreya was pleased. He placed his hand of blessing on his head with his lotus-like hands. He knew that Revannath is the incarnation of Chamsanarayana among the Navanarayanas. However, at that moment, he did not give him complete grace. Because a thought was in his mind that as long as a soul is not inclined towards the path of devotion, it is useless to give complete knowledge. First, devotion must be awakened; after that, knowledge and detachment are obtained automatically. Therefore, he gave Revannath the art of only one Siddhi (supernatural power). Even by that small grace, Revannath was extremely delighted. He bowed at the feet of Dattatreya. Dattatreya moved forward, and Revannath remained satisfied with that obtained Siddhi. After this, Revannath went to the fields and began chanting mantras. By the power of those mantras, ‘Siddhi’ appeared directly before him. She asked—“For what purpose have I been called?” To test her, Revannath asked to convert the heap of grain into gold. In an instant, that heap of gold was created. From that day on, Siddhi began to stay in his service in a secret form. Revannath gave up farming. Wealth showered in his house. His father was astonished to see this and began to consider him an incarnate being. Further, Revannath began giving the people of the village food of their choice, and distributing clothes and wealth. The diseases of the sick also began to be cured. Because of that, he became famous as ‘Revansiddha’.
revannathText3: One day Machindranath came to that village. Hearing the greatness of Revansiddha from the people, he decided to test him. Using his Yogic power, he created lions, tigers, and other animals and played with them. Seeing this miracle, Revannath was astonished. He requested Siddhi that he too should get such power. Then Siddhi told him that this is not possible without Brahma-jnana (supreme knowledge). Therefore, Revannath resolved to worship Dattatreya again. He went to the previous spot and began to perform severe penance—he gave up food and water, and began to live on leaves. His body became lean like a piece of wood. Seeing his condition, Machindranath went to Dattatreya and told him the entire account. Dattatreya came there with Machindranath. He picked up Revannath into his lap and gave him the mantra initiation. His ignorance was destroyed and he became fully wise. After that, he was given initiation into all scriptures, weapons, and the Nathpanth. Upon attaining perfection, Revannath held a large ceremony. All the gods were present. Later he set out on a pilgrimage.
revannathText4: In that period, he had a meal at a Brahmin's house. All the children of that Brahmin used to die; the seventh son also died. Revannath, getting angry at Yama, decided to revive that boy. He kept the boy's body safe by applying sacred ash with the Amara-mantra and went to Yamapuri himself. Yamadharma welcomed him with respect. Revannath asked for all seven of the Brahmin's sons back. Then Yama said that the authority for this task lies with Shankara, therefore he should go to Kailash. Returning from Yamapuri, Revannath set out for Kailash. On the way, the Shivaganas stopped him. They questioned him—“Who are you? Where are you going?” Then Revannath said fearlessly, “I am Revannath. Shankara has stolen and brought a Brahmin's son, I have come to punish him and take that son back.” Upon hearing these harsh words, the Shivaganas became enraged. They mocked him. But Revannath's wrath flared up. He used the Sparshastra (touch weapon) and threw sacred ash, and in an instant, thirteen hundred Shivaganas were pinned to the ground—motionless, helpless! Seeing this terrible state, the terrified Ganas told the whole account to Shankara. Shankara immediately sent the Ashtabhairavas for war. The Bhairavas attacked with a massive army. But Revannath defeated their weapons and made them exhausted too. Finally, Shankara himself arrived on the battlefield riding Nandi. Revannath thought that it is not right to have a long war with Shankara. He used the Vatakarsana Astra—and by that influence, Shankara's breath stopped, and he fell from Nandi; the Ashtabhairavas also became unconscious. Upon learning of this calamity, Vishnu rushed there. He reasoned with Revannath—“Why did you do all this?” Then Revannath said, “The Brahmin's son has been killed. I will bring him back to life. For that, I have stopped Shankara's life-breath.” Vishnu said that all seven sons of that Brahmin are in his possession. He gave those seven life-essences to Revannath. Then Revannath revived Shankara and freed all the Ganas. Everyone bowed to his prowess. After that, he returned to earth. Going to the Brahmin, he crushed the dead boy's body into seven parts and prepared seven statues. By the power of the Sanjivani mantra, those seven statues obtained life—they began to cry! He handed those seven children over to their parents and gave them names. Further, they all became great Siddhas.
naganathText1: A portion of the brilliant seed of the creator Brahmadev fell onto the Earth. By a mysterious coincidence of destiny, that brilliant spark fell on the head of a female serpent, and she carried it in her womb. It was not merely a seed — it was the incarnation of Airhotra Narayana among the Nine Narayanas. Day by day, the fetus grew. This matter came to the attention of the great Sage Astika, who knew things through divine vision. He saw in meditation that from the womb of this serpent, a great Siddha, Yogi, and benefactor of the people would be born in the future — whom the world would know as Vatsiddha Naganath.
naganathText2: However, at that time, a terrible event was taking place on Earth. King Janamejaya was performing the 'Sarpa Satra' sacrifice — where countless serpents were being offered as sacrifices in the sacrificial fire. A crisis had befallen the entire serpent race. Knowing this, Sage Astika called the female serpent and said with compassion, “O Mother of Serpents, do not be afraid. There is a divine incarnation in your womb. But the times are difficult. A great crisis is coming. Protect yourself and that divine fetus.” The serpent became terrified. She requested, “Show me a safe place.” Then the Sage showed her a hollow in a huge, ancient Banyan tree (Vatvruksha) nearby, saying, “Take shelter here and be at peace.” The serpent hid in that hollow. Sage Astika provided divine protection to that Banyan tree through his yogic power and then left for Hastinapur. Time moved on. Nine months were completed. At that sacred moment, the serpent laid an egg. That egg remained safe inside the Banyan tree for a long time. Divine consciousness was moving within that egg — Airhotra Narayana was manifesting in that fetus. The time was ripe, and the egg hatched. From it emerged a brilliant, divine child — whose body glowed with light. But at that moment, there was no one near the child. At that time, a Brahmin named Koshadharma, a student of the Atharvaveda but extremely poor and plagued by his poverty, used to go to the forest to collect Banyan leaves for his daily survival. On that day too, he reached that Banyan tree for leaves as usual. But suddenly, the sound of a piteous cry reached his ears. He stopped. He began to look around—but saw no one. Yet the sound was clear… that of a newborn child. For a moment, he thought it was an illusion. But his heart said—“This is indeed the voice of a child.” Suddenly, a divine voice echoed from the sky—“O Koshadharma! There is a divine child in the hollow of this Banyan tree. Whatever object he touches will turn to gold. And if this child goes to your house, your poverty will be destroyed.” Just then, a divine arrow came and struck the Banyan tree… and that massive tree crashed to the ground. As the tree fell, the brilliant child hidden in its hollow was revealed. The gods bowed to the child and told Koshadharma—“You are fortunate. This child is none other than ‘Vatsiddha Naganath’. He was born from the womb of a serpent named Padmini, and the Banyan tree has protected him. In the future, he will become a great Siddha and the lord of Yogis.” Hearing this, tears of joy welled up in Koshadharma's eyes. He lovingly picked up the divine child and brought him home. When his wife, Suradevi, saw this child, her heart was filled with love. She said in wonder—“It is as if the moon or the sun itself has descended!” She took the child in her arms… and at that moment, milk began to flow from her breasts spontaneously—as if motherhood itself had awakened. In that joy, she bathed the child, placed him in the cradle, and named him “Vatsiddha Naganath”. From that day on, happiness, contentment, and divinity resided in that house. Time moved on… Naganath began to grow up. In his seventh year, Koshadharma performed his thread ceremony (Upanayana) according to the rites and set him on the path of Vedic studies.
naganathText3: One day, on the sacred banks of the Bhagirathi, in front of Kashi Vishweshwara, a miraculous and divine scene was unfolding… small but brilliant Vatsiddha Naganath was gathering children of his age and playing an extraordinary game. That game was not simple—it was the “Game of Food Donation”. Naganath was seating the children in rows and serving them food from his imagination. “Take… take more…” he was urging them lovingly, and the surprise was that those children were also saying with satisfaction, “Enough, our stomachs are full!” At this very time, Shri Dattatreya was passing by. He saw this miraculous game and was surprised. “How can the stomach be filled with fake food?” This thought came to his mind and he smiled gently. To test the heart of this child, he himself took the form of a child and went to stand among those children. He said, “I am a guest… I am very hungry… give me something to eat.” Hearing this, the other children did not recognize him. Some tried to chase him away, some raised sticks, and some ran with stones. But at that time, Naganath came forward. Stopping all the children, he said calmly, “One should never chase away whoever comes new to our group. One should treat a guest as God and serve him.” Saying this, he seated the child with honor. He arranged for bathing, worship, rituals, and a meal through his imagination. He began to urge him lovingly, “Eat slowly… do not hurry… ask for whatever you want…” Dattatreya was extremely pleased with Naganath's innocent spirit of service. A thought came to his mind—“This is no ordinary boy; he must be some great Yogi from a previous birth.” He meditated and saw his past life and, being pleased with his merits, granted him a divine siddhi. The result of that siddhi was that whatever item Naganath named, that item began to manifest physically. After that day, his game truly turned into reality. When Naganath played with the children, six-flavored food was actually created. The children would go home satisfied and therefore began refusing to eat at home.
naganathText4: The parents were surprised. When they asked the children, the children said—“We eat at Naganath's place and come.” Initially, no one believed this. But when they went to the banks of the Bhagirathi and saw it for themselves, they had the direct experience—Naganath places his hand on the ground and the desired food manifests! This miraculous news spread everywhere. The fame of Naganath began to be heralded in every village. Finally, this news reached his father, Koshadharma. One day he seated Naganath on his lap and asked lovingly, “Child, how do you do all this?” Then Naganath began to answer calmly, “Father, once we children were playing by the river. Then a boy came. Everyone chased him away, but I served him. That was Shri Dattatreya. He was pleased with me and gave me this siddhi. Since that day, whatever item is named by my mouth, that item is created.” Hearing this, Koshadharma was overjoyed. He remembered the divine voice and recognized the divinity of his son. From that day on, the great tradition of continuous food donation, service to guests, and public welfare began at the hands of Naganath, and Vatsiddha Naganath gradually began to become famous as a great Siddha, Yogi, and a brilliant saint in the Nath tradition.
naganathText5: One day Naganath asked his father, “What is the true purpose of these miraculous things happening through me? And who was Dattatreya?” Then the father said that Dattatreya is an incarnation of all three gods—Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh. You are fortunate that he met you and gave you the siddhi. But meeting him is very difficult—he grants vision only of his own will. Hearing this, Naganath resolved to have the vision of Dattatreya. He left home without telling anyone and began searching in many pilgrimage sites. Finally, he reached Kolhapur and inquired with the people. Then the people said that Dattatreya comes here, but no one can recognize him—he comes in different forms to ask for alms. Naganath asked if he does not take alms elsewhere. Upon that, people said that Dattatreya takes food only in Kolhapur. If he does not get food here, he will fast, but he will not go to another village. In his view, the food of this place is extremely sacred. Naganath thought that if he did not let any cooking happen in the village and invited all the people to eat in one place, Dattatreya would not find food elsewhere and would automatically come here. But keeping in mind that he would not eat food from his hand, he resolved to catch his feet once he recognized him. After this, he went to the temple of Lakshmi and took a room from the priest and began staying there.
naganathText6: After a few days, the thought of arranging a meal for the entire village came to his mind. He requested the priest for help. The priest said, from where will you get the food materials required for such a large meal? Upon that, Naganath said that I will provide all the materials, you just make the arrangements. Finally, with the power of his siddhi, Naganath collected grains, oil, sugar, and all other necessary items in large quantities and showed them to the priest. After that, he invited people of all castes, from kings to the poor, along with their families for the meal. It was said that no one should cook in the village. Arrangements for meals and snacks were made for everyone in the morning, afternoon, and in between. Therefore, everyone in the village had prepared food at home and no one was lighting a stove. This grand ceremony lasted for a full month.
naganathText7: On the very first day, Dattatreya came to the village for alms, but food was not found anywhere. People began telling him, “There is a big meal in the village today, go there.” But even though Dattatreya asked for alms in different forms, he did not take that food. Because it was food prepared through siddhi. Finally, he went and saw for himself and understood that this large arrangement had been made by Vatsiddha Naganath—the same one to whom he had given the siddhi many years ago. He realized that Naganath had made this effort just for his vision. Still, Dattatreya fasted that day and left. He would come to the village every day and ask for only simple alms, and if he did not get that either, he would go elsewhere and eat. In this way, a full month passed. Naganath began to think, why is the vision of Dattatreya still not happening? So he asked the villagers if anyone comes to ask for alms in the village. Then people said that a beggar comes every day, but he takes only simple alms and does not accept your food. Then Naganath said if that beggar comes again, inform me immediately. Also, do not give him dry alms, give only the food prepared here, and if he refuses, call me. The next time Dattatreya came to ask for alms, the people tried to give him Naganath's food, but he refused it. He did not take dry alms either. Immediately this news was given to Naganath. He came running there, and as soon as he saw that beggar, he fell at his feet and bowed. Naganath requested with great devotion. Seeing his true feeling, Dattatreya was pleased. He picked him up, wiped the tears from his eyes, and gave him a mantra. At that moment, Naganath attained self-knowledge and his ignorance disappeared. He understood the true form of Dattatreya and was overwhelmed with joy.
naganathText8: After this, Dattatreya told him that you are an incarnation of Narayana from a previous birth, hence the siddhi was given to you. Later both went to Kashi, and from there went further to Badrikashram and met Lord Shiva. Shankara asked Dattatreya to give Naganath the initiation into the Nathpanth, and Dattatreya taught him. In six months, they made Naganath proficient in all sciences and arts. Later, Naganath performed penance for twelve years and obtained many siddhis. Finally, Dattatreya ordered him to go on a pilgrimage. Naganath accordingly set out on the journey and Dattatreya moved forward on his way. While on pilgrimage, Naganath came to Balaghat and began living in the forest. Because of his fame, people from nearby villages began coming for his vision. Gradually many people began living near him and that place was named “Wadwal”.
naganathText9: One day Machindranath came to that village while on pilgrimage. He learned of Naganath's fame, so he went for his vision. But the disciples at the door stopped him and said, “Permission must be taken first.” Hearing this, Machindranath became very angry. He felt that there should be no such obstacle to the vision of saints. He rebuked the disciples. Then many of Naganath's disciples came there, but Machindranath stopped them in their tracks with his yogic power and taught them a lesson. Those disciples cried out in fear. Naganath was sitting in meditation in the monastery. Hearing the shouting outside, his meditation was broken and he came out in anger. He saw that his disciples were being beaten and Machindranath was teaching them a lesson. Naganath immediately used his sciences to free the disciples and started a confrontation with Machindranath. A terrible war took place between the two—powers like the Parvatastra, Vajrastra, and Sarpastra were used. Finally, Naganath used the Sarpastra to create large snakes that injured Machindranath. Machindranath found himself in a crisis and remembered his guru—Dattatreya. Hearing this, Naganath became doubtful. He asked Machindranath, and Machindranath told him that they were disciples of Dattatreya. Knowing this, Naganath's anger subsided. He immediately removed the snakes and asked Machindranath's forgiveness. Treating him like an elder brother, he took him to the monastery and kept him with respect for a month.
naganathText10: One day Machindranath asked Naganath what the purpose was behind stopping people for vision. Naganath said he did so so that meditation would not be broken. Upon that, Machindranath said that this is not right—people come with devotion, they should not be stopped. Accepting this, Naganath opened the monastery for everyone. After this, the crowd of people increased. By Naganath's grace, even dead persons began to be brought to life. This caused a great stir and the order of death began to be disrupted. Finally, this matter reached Brahmadev. Brahmadev himself came and praised Naganath and asked him to stop this work, and Naganath accepted it.
charapatinathText1: In the past, during the marriage of Goddess Parvati, all the gods had gathered. At that time, a desire arose in the mind of Lord Brahmadev and his seed was shed. From it, many sages were created, and a portion of it fell into a river and got stuck in the grass. Later, the essence of Pippalayan Narayana entered it, and from that, a divine child was born—he was Charapatinath.
charapatinathText2: A Brahmin named Satyashrava found this brilliant child. Initially, he was afraid, but Narada explained to him that this is a divine child. Then Satyashrava took him home and raised him. His wife, Chandra, also accepted him joyfully. Charapati grew up and began to progress in education. Later, Narada devised a plan to create a sense of detachment (vairagya) in his mind towards worldly life. In one instance, he was deeply hurt because his father struck him in anger, and he left home to sit in a temple. Then Narada appeared again in another form and motivated him to renounce the world. Charapati and “Kulamb” (Narada's form) both went to Badrikashram. There they met Dattatreya and Machindranath. Narada revealed his true identity. Charapati fell at their feet and requested for a Guru. Dattatreya gave him a mantra, and he immediately attained self-knowledge. Thereafter, Lord Shiva also appeared and blessed him. Later, Dattatreya taught him all sciences, weaponry, and yogic practices. Charapatinath then performed severe penance for twelve years, obtained many siddhis, and prepared many disciples. After that, he continued his spiritual work by visiting various pilgrimage sites.
ovi15: तीर्थे करितां अपरिमित ॥ सच्छिष्य नव झाले त्यांत ॥ ते नवशिष्य प्रख्यातवंत ॥ सिद्धकळा जाणती ॥८९॥ राघवसिद्ध बाळसिद्ध ॥ गोकाटसिद्ध जाबुसिद्ध ॥ नैमित्यिक सारेंद्वक हुक्ष प्रसिद्ध ॥ द्वारभैरव रणसिद्ध तो ॥१९०॥ ऐसे चरपटाचे नवसिद्ध वर्ण ॥ शाबरी विद्येंत असती पूर्ण ॥ चौर्‍यायशीं सिद्ध नवांपासून ॥ उदयवंत पावले ॥९१॥ जोगी शारंगी निजानंद ॥ नैननिरंजन यदु प्रसिद्ध ॥ गैवनक्षुद्र कास्त सिद्ध ॥ रेवणनाथाचे असती पैं ॥९२॥ उरेश सुरेश धुरेश कुहर ॥ केशमर्दन सुद्धकपूर ॥ भटेंद्र आणि कटभ्रवा साबर ॥ हे नवसिद्ध भर्तरीनाथाचे ॥९३॥ दक्षेंद्र आणि अनिर्वा अपरोक्ष ॥ कामुकार्णव सहनसिद्ध प्रसिद्ध ॥ दक्षलायन देवसिद्ध ॥ पाक्षेंद्र साक्ष मच्छिंद्राचे सिद्ध हे ॥९४॥ निर्णयार्णव हरदंतान ॥ भोमान हुक्षे कृष्णपलायन ॥ हेमा क्षेत्रांत रत्नागर नाम ॥ गोरक्षाचे हे असती ॥९५॥ विनयभास्कर दत्तघात ॥ पवनभार्गव सुक्षार्णव यथार्थ ॥ कविटशवी वधम प्रोक्षित ॥ नव जालिंदराचे हे असती ॥९६॥ शारुक वालुक शरभ सहन ॥ प्रोक्षितशैर्म कोकिल नाम ॥ कोस्मितवाच संपति नवही पूर्ण ॥ कान्हिपाचे हे असती ॥९७॥ यापरी चौरंगीचे सहा सिद्ध ॥ लोम भ्रातरक चिरकालवृन्द ॥ नारायण काळिका साव्रजी प्रसिद्ध ॥ चौरंगीचे असती पैं ॥९८॥ मीननाथ अडबंगीनाथ ॥ यांचे सहा सिद्ध सिद्धिवंत ॥ सुलक्षा लुक्ष मोक्षार्णव समर्थ ॥ द्वार भद्राक्ष सहावा ॥९९॥ एकूण चौर्‍यायशीं सिद्धांचा झाडा पूर्ण ॥ ग्रंथीं वदला धुंडीनंदन ॥ मालू नरकिमयागार ॥ सदा परिसोत भाविक चतुर ॥ अष्टत्रिंशततिमोऽध्याय गोड हा ॥२०१॥
machindranathText28: In this way, the tradition of the eighty-four Siddhas was completed. The stories of these great Siddhas and their works have been mentioned by Dhundinandan in his book 'Navnath Bhaktisar'. The tradition of all these Siddhas is a divine spiritual heritage, which devotees should listen to with faith, understand, and practice in their lives.
charapatinathText3: After completing all the pilgrimages on Earth, a desire arose in Charapatinath's mind to see the pilgrimages in Heaven and the Netherworld (Patala) as well. Therefore, he went to Badrikashram, had the vision of Lord Shiva, and went to Heaven through his yogic power. He first reached Lord Brahmadev's Satyaloka. Brahmadev welcomed him and asked the reason for his arrival. Charapatinath stayed there for some time. Meanwhile, one day when Narada went to Amarpuri (Indraloka), Indra casually said to him in jest, 'Welcome, Narada of Discord'. Upon hearing those words, Narada became very angry. Resolving in his mind to bring that discord upon Indra, Narada left from there. After a few days, Narada plotted to humiliate and distress Indra through Charapatinath. He took Charapatinath along to Indra's garden. There, Charapatinath ate fruits and plucked flowers. As this began to happen daily, the garden started being destroyed. Finally, the guards caught him, but Charapatinath defeated them with his yogic power. When Indra received this news, he sent the celestial army, but it too was rendered ineffective. Then Indra sought Shiva's help. Shiva and his army came, but Charapatinath defeated them as well. Thereafter, Vishnu also came for war, but he subdued him too. Not only that, but even Vishnu's Sudarshana Chakra came under his control. Seeing this state, Brahmadev became worried. He explained to Charapatinath that all these gods are necessary for the world. Then Charapatinath withdrew his power and revived all the gods with the Sanjivani mantra. After this, all the gods praised him and went to their respective places. Narada taunted Indra, due to which Indra also admitted his mistake. Finally, Charapatinath completed his pilgrimages of Heaven and the Netherworld. He went to King Bali's house, bowed to Lord Vamana, and then returned to Earth again.
machindranathText29: Indra felt deeply insulted by the defeat inflicted by Charapatinath. He was dejected at heart. He expressed his distress to Brihaspati, saying that although Charapatinath is young, he is extremely brilliant, and has even defeated Shiva and Vishnu—no one possesses such power. Especially, it is not known how he obtained the “Vatakarsana Vidya”. Some remedy must be found so that we too may obtain that knowledge; otherwise, we will have to accept his servitude. Hearing this, Brihaspati suggested a plan. He said that a Somayaga (sacrifice) should be organized to call the Naths here. On that pretext, Charapatinath and other Naths will come. Then, by remaining in their service and pleasing them, your purpose can be achieved. Indra agreed to this plan. But the question was—who would go to bring the Naths? Then Brihaspati said that Uparikshavasu (who is the father of Machindranath) among the Ashtavasus is suitable for this. If he is sent, he will surely bring the Naths. Then Indra called Uparikshavasu, explained his plan, and sent him with a celestial vehicle (Vimana) to bring the Naths.
machindranathText30: Uparikshavasu came to Badrikashram and met Machindranath. At that time, Nath members like Gorakshanath, Dharmanath, Chauranginath, Kanifnath, Gopichand, Jalandharnath, Adabanginath, etc., were present there. As soon as Uparikshavasu arrived, Machindranath stood up and placed his head at his feet. Thereafter, Uparikshavasu conveyed Indra's message before everyone and requested the Navnaths to come to Amarpuri (Amravati). By counseling them, he obtained their consent to come. After this, all the jogis including Jalandharnath, Kanifnath, Chauranginath, Machindranath, Gorakshanath, Adabanginath, Gopichand, etc., sat in the Vimana. While traveling, they first came to Helapattan in Gauda-Bengal. There, Gopichand took his mother along. Then they went to the village of Wadwal and took Vatsiddha Naganath along after counseling him. Further, they went to the banks of the Gomati River and took Bhartruhari from there. Then they went to the banks of the Tamraparni River and took Charapatinath with them. Proceeding further, they went to Vitgaon in the Pune region and brought Revannath. In this way, the Navnaths, along with eighty-four Siddhas, sat in the Vimana and went to Amravati for the Somayagna.
machindranathText31: As soon as the Naths' Vimana arrived, Indra himself came forward to welcome them. Speaking very humbly, he placed his head at their feet. Then he took all the Naths to his residence, seated them on thrones, and worshipped them with Shodashopachara rituals. At that time, all the gods stood before them with joy. Then Indra presented his purpose of performing the Somayagna before everyone and requested them to suggest a suitable place for the sacrifice. Then Machindranath and Brihaspati, after deliberation, chose the Atavya forest in Simhaladvipa. Due to the cool shade and plenty of water in that place, it was deemed suitable for the sacrifice. Thereafter, Indra thought of sitting for the sacrifice himself along with his wife. Arrangements were made such that Brihaspati would chant the mantras and the Navnaths would offer oblations into the sacrificial pit. This forest was on the border of Kilotle. Therefore, Machindranath remembered Minanath of that place. He asked Uparikshavasu to bring Minanath and others. Uparikshavasu brought them, and Machindranath kept them there. Machindranath further taught Minanath the pursuit of knowledge. Meanwhile, Brihaspati advised Indra that instead of sitting himself for the sacrifice, he should have Uparikshavasu sit. Therefore, Indra tied the sacrificial bracelet to Uparikshavasu and began to supervise himself. Indra himself was providing all the materials required for the sacrifice. Indra served with great devotion and promptness. Seeing his sincere feeling, all the Naths, sages, and gods were extremely pleased.
machindranathText32: While Machindranath was teaching Minanath the Vidya, Indra took the form of a peacock (Mayura) and secretly sat on a tree, learning the Vatakarsana Mantra Vidya. As soon as he obtained that Vidya, Indra was extremely satisfied. The sacrifice continued for one year, and during that time, Machindranath was teaching the Vidya to Minanath.
machindranathText33: After the sacrifice was over, Machindranath sat for the foremost worship (Agrapuja). After the formal worship was completed, Indra also worshipped all the other Naths and honored them with clothes and jewelry. After all the Naths sat on golden thrones (Kanakasanas), Indra humbly joined his hands and requested, “An injustice has been committed by me—while you were teaching Minanath the Vidya, I learned it secretly. Please forgive me and bless me so that the Vidya may bear fruit.” Hearing this, all the Naths became angry and cursed Indra, saying, “You have taken the Vidya through deceit, therefore it will be fruitless.” Hearing this curse, Uparikshavasu and Brihaspati requested the Naths and calmed them. The gods also mediated. Finally, the Naths gave a counter-curse (Ushapa) that, “Indra should perform penance for twelve years and not harass the Nathpanth; then only will the Vidya bear fruit.” After this, all the Naths returned to Earth by Vimana and began their pilgrimages again. Machindranath, after asking Minanath in Kilotle, took him along as well. He delivered Mainavati to Helapattan. Minanath had three Siddha disciples. Further, all the Naths went in different directions to perform pilgrimages. Indra performed severe penance on the Sahyadri mountains for twelve years. While performing Mantrayoga, the water he released became a stream and flowed to join the Bhimarathi. That stream was named “Indrayani”. After completing his penance, Indra went back to Amravati.
machindranathText34: The Navnaths performed pilgrimages for a long time. They were wandering in manifest form until the Shaka year 1710. Afterward, they became hidden (Gupta). Kanifa stayed in a monastery. Near him, but on the upper side, stayed Machindranath, who is called 'Byba'. Jalandharnath is called 'Janpir'; he stayed on Garbhagiri, and on the lower side of him stayed Gahininath, also called 'Gairipir'. Naganath stayed at Wadwal and Revannath stayed at Vitgaon. Charapatinath, Chauranginath, and Adabanginath are still performing pilgrimages in hidden form. Bhartari (Bhartruhari) stayed in the netherworld (Patala). Minanath went to reside in Heaven. Gorakshanath stayed in the ashram of Shri Dattatreya on Girinar mountain. Gopichand and Dharmanath went to Vaikuntha. Then Vishnu sent a Vimana and took Mainavati to Vaikuntha. The Nathpanth flourished from the eighty-four Siddhas.
machindranathText35: Finally, Malukavi says that this chronicle of the Navnaths ends here. Whoever keeps faith in this book will benefit, and whoever criticizes it will suffer grief. This “Shri Navnath Bhakti Kathasagar” book was completed by Malukavi in the Shaka year 1741, on the day of Jyeshtha Shuddha Pratipada, after praying to Shri Dattatreya and the Navnaths.
machindranathInNepalText1: Grierson and Bagchi have narrated the prevalent legends of Nepal. In Nepalese Buddhist tales, Machindranath is identified as Avalokiteshvara. Machindranath used to live on a mountain that was difficult to climb. It became hard for Gorakshanath to climb that mountain, so he attempted to do so by binding the nine Nagas (serpents) together. The consequence of this was that it did not rain in Nepal for twelve years. King Narendra Deva's guru, Buddhadatta, understood the reason and went to Kapotaka Mountain to bring Avalokiteshvara. Avalokiteshvara was pleased and gave Buddhadatta a mantra. He also guided him that because of this mantra, the Nagas would come toward those who chant it. Upon returning, he performed the ritual of this mantra. Avalokiteshvara transformed into a bee (Bhringa) and descended into Nepal due to the power of the mantra, resulting in a downpour of rain in Nepal. As a mark of this, a pilgrimage (Yatra) of Machindranath is still held at a place called Bungm.
machindranathInNepalText2: There is also a story that because the people of Nepal did not accord proper respect to Gorakshanath, he became angry and imprisoned the clouds, stopping the rainfall there. For twelve years, there was a drought in Nepal. At that very time, Machindranath arrived in Nepal; when Goraksh rose to greet him, the clouds were released and the natural cycle resumed.
machindranathInNepalText3: The significance of Machindranath in Nepal is immense. There is another story regarding this: on the eastern bank of the Bagmati River, there are temples of Gorakshanath and Machindranath. Since Machindranath's worldly pleasures were ceased, the tradition of marrying the Nepaleshwara of that place to a Brahmin girl was started upon Goraksh's command. These women who serve the monastery are regarded as 'Nathini'. The festival of Machindranath begins from Vaishakh Shuddha Pratipada. After a seven-day chariot procession (Rath Yatra), the idol is taken back to the Bagmati River. This auspicious day is named 'Gudrizhad'. 'Gudri' means a blanket. On this day, the blanket of the Naths is shaken out and shown. It signifies that the Naths brought nothing with them; they exist in a state of absolute detachment (Shunyavritti).
warakariTitle: Maharashtra's Heritage of Nathpanth: The Warakari Sampradaya
abhangText1: || Adinath is the Guru of all Siddhas | Machindra is his chief disciple |
abhangText2: | Machindra gave the realization to Goraksha | Goraksha bestowed his grace upon Gahini |
abhangText3: | By the grace of Gahini, Nivritti became the giver | Jnanadeva realized the true essence ||
warakariText1: The world-revered Mauli Shri Sant Dnyaneshwar Maharaj composed the above Abhang while describing his eminent Guru lineage.
warakariText2: In the Shiva-worshipping Nath Sampradaya, the inclusion of the Vishnu element is seen in the form of Machindranath. Dnyaneshwar Maharaj, the pioneer of Nathpanth in Maharashtra, is considered an incarnation of Vishnu, while Nivritti Nath is commonly believed to be an incarnation of Shiva. In this way, a broad vision of the unity and coordination of Shiva and Vishnu occurs in Nathpanth. Consequently, almost all religious sects or communities in Maharashtra are linked to Nathpanth for one reason or another.
warakariText3: The Nath Sampradaya, coming through the lineage of Adinath—Machindranath—Gorakshanath—Gahininath—Nivruttinath, developed in various aspects in Maharashtra. The seed of Krishna-bhakti rooted in Nathpanth blossomed and grew in the hearts of Namdevraya, Narhari Sonar, Gora Kumbhar, Janabai, and others during the time of Dnyaneshwar himself. The expansion of this tiny sapling is seen reaching the heavens in the form of saints like Eknath, Tukaram, Niloba, and others. This branch of the Bhagavat Sampradaya, i.e., the Warakari sect, which originated from Nathpanth, expanded greatly and became popular in Maharashtra.
warakariText4: In the period following Machindra and Goraksha, the development of Saguna Bhakti (devotion to a manifest God) through local languages also had a firm foundation in Nathpanthi philosophy and spiritual practices. Although the Shiva of the Nathpanthis is a form of light beyond Saguna-Nirguna and Sakara-Nirakara, many saints have testified that the same principle experienced by Yogis in meditation manifests in a beautiful Saguna form during Hari-Kirtan and Nama-Smaran (chanting the divine name).
abhangText4: Adinath revealed the seed of knowledge to Uma | Machindra attained it in a state of natural bliss || 1 ||
abhangText5: The same seal of love was given to Goraksha | Full grace was bestowed upon Gahininath || 2 ||
abhangText6: Heated by detachment, cooled by love | Attained the treasure of peace and happiness || 3 ||
abhangText7: Wandering the earth without conflict or doubt | Bliss became steady in the heart || 4 ||
abhangText8: A vessel of renunciation, the mouth of Vedic continuity | Bestowing complete and absolute devotion || 5 ||
abhangText9: Nivritti says Gahini bestowed full grace | This lineage is sanctified by the name of Krishna || 6 ||
warakariText5: While Adinath Shankar was imparting knowledge to Parvati, Machindranath, who was in a state of 'Sahaj-sthiti' (natural meditation) in the Ocean of Milk, attained that knowledge. Machindranath passed the same 'Prem-nam-mudra' (seal of the loving name) to Gorakshanath, and from Gorakshanath, that grace was received by Gahininath. Those who possess intense detachment and love in their hearts attain the treasure of peace and happiness. In the heart of one who has no duality or doubt and wanders continuously for public welfare, the Supreme Soul in the form of blissful joy resides. To the one who is completely detached and lives according to the Vedas, the Supreme Soul grants complete and exclusive knowledge.
warakariText6: Nivruttinath says that Satguru Gahininath showed grace and gave this secret knowledge to him, due to which his entire lineage became sanctified by the name of Krishna. Nivruttinath states that he received this loving 'nam-mudra' from Gahininath. Similarly, Dnyaneshwar Maharaj and other saints are frequently seen mentioning that they received such a 'Prem-mudra' from the Nathpanth.
